식물유전체재조합 연구실: 교차(crossover) 조절 연구와
식물 유전체 디자인
​
​
인류는 약 1만 년 전 식물을 재배하기 시작하며 육종(breeding)을 통해 식물을 개량해 왔다. F1 hybrid 잡종 강세와 교배 육종의 녹색혁명(Green Revolution)은 인류의 식량 안보와 보건, 그리고 평화에 기여했다. 멘델의 유전법칙, DNA의 발견에 이은 차세대 DNA 시퀀싱 기술(next-generation sequencing, NGS), 유전자 가위 기술(CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing), 기계 학습(machine learning), AI 등의 혁신적인 연구 기술 진보는 감수분열(meiosis)동안 교차 현상에 대한 이해는 물론
교차 조절, MiMe (Mitosis instead of Meiosis), hapoloid inducer, synthetic apomixis
을 통해 식물 개량과 육종을 보다 가속화하고 있다. 우리는 현재
식물 유전체 디자인 시대
(링크
-대학신문기사
)
에 살고 있다.
​
식물 교차 패턴 연구(Mechanism of Meiotic Crossover Patterning in Plants)
​
식물유전체재조합 연구실은
모델 식물 애기장대와 토마토에서 교차(crossover)의 분자적 기전을 연구
한다. 식물 감수분열은 꽃의 암술, 수술의 meiocyte에서 일어나며 haploid인 sperm, egg cell를 만든다. 이들 반수체 세포들은 수정을 통해 다음 세대의 diploid 식물이 된다. 특히 감수분열에서는 상동 염색체(homologous chromosome) 사이에
교차(crossing over=crossover=CO)
가 일어나 자손의 유전적 다양성을 증가시키며 식물 육종에 중요한 역할을 한다. 교차는 많은 수의 DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs)에 의해서 시작하지만 이들 DSBs 중
약 5% 정도만이 DBS 수선 과정을 거쳐 교차
가 된다. 따라서, 상동 염색체상의 교차 수는 염색체 분리를 위해 1개는 필수적이지만 그 이상은 억제되어 1개 또는 2개가 주로 일어나며 3개인 경우도 드물다 (동.식물, ~1.5-2.0 COs per chromosome pair). 또한 상동 염색체 사이에 드물게 두 개의 교차가 발생하더라도 두 개의 교차는
교차 간섭(crossover interference)
현상으로 인해 서로 멀리 떨어져서 발생한다. 즉 두 개의 교차가 가깝게 일어나는 일은 거의 없다. 또한 교차는 pericentromere에서 더욱 드물게 일어난다. 이러한 교차 수와 빈도, 교차 패턴은 교차 촉진자(pro-crossover factors), 교차 억제자(anti-crossover factors) 및 epigenetic factor들(H3K9me2/non-CG methylation,
H2A.W:
PNAS
)에 의해 조절된다. 따라서
식물 교차의 패턴 연구
를 통한 교차 수와 위치 조절은 apomixis, haploid inducer, reverse breeding과 함께 새로운 육종 기술 개발에 매우 중요한 기여를 한다.  특히, 교차 간섭 현상은 20세기 초에 발견됐지만 분자적 기전은 오랫동안 미궁이었다. 하지만 최근에 synaptonemal complex의 components와 pro-crossover E3 ligase HEI10이 교차 간섭을 매개하고 있음이 밝혀졌다. 우리 연구실은
교차 수와 교차 간섭을 조절하는 새로운 교차 조절 인자(HCR1, HCR2, HCR3, HCR7)를 유전학적으로 발굴하고 최첨단 유전체학, 세포학, 분자생물학적 연구 기법들을 통해 교차 패턴의 기초 연구를 수행
중이며, 이를
토마토의 교차 조절에도 적용
하고 있다.
​
최첨단 교차 재조합 연구 방법
새로운
교차율 증가 돌연변이 발굴 및 연구:
교차 재조합의 분자적 기전을 밝히기 위해서 우리는 교차 빈도 증가(
high crossover rate, hcr
) 또는 감소하는 돌연변이들을 찾는 유전학적 스크리닝을 수행해오고 있다. 특히 형광 종자 및 형광 꽃가루 교차 리포터 시스템(seed or pollen fluorescence tagged lines, FTLs)을 활용하고 딥러닝 기반
이미지 분석을 통해 교차 빈도를 정교하고 신속하고 대량으로 분석
이 가능하다. 돌연변이원으로는 EMS, activation-tagging 을 활용한다 (
hcr3:Nature Plants
,
hcr2:EMBO J
,
hcr1:Nature Plants
)
​
고해상도 유전체 수준의 교차 지도 작성 (High-resolution Genome-wide Crossover Mapping):
short-read와 long-read next-generation sequencing 기술을 활용하여 96개 F2 식물체들을 동시에 시퀀싱하여 교차 위치를 정확히 탐지한다 (genotyping-by-sequencing,
GBS
; Nanopore seq를 이용한
COmapper:
New Phytologist
).
​
Immuno-cytology:
교차 과정은 감수분열 동안 염색체의 움직임과 구조 변화와 연관되어 있다. DSB 형성 시 leptotene은 axis-loop 구조를 만들고, 이후 DSB 수선 시 zygotene의 상동염색체는 pairing이 일어나고 pachytene에서는 상동염색체간 synaptonemal complex를 통해 synapsis를 이룬다. 교차는 pachytene 말기와 diplotene, diakinesis에서 MLH1의 immunostaining을 통해 확인이 가능하다. 또한 axis element, DSB foci, ZMMs (pro-crossover factors)들 역시 immunocytology을 통해 확인한다.
​
​
Genomic approaches:
SPO11-oligo sequencing, pollen-typing, mei-ChIP seq, Nuc-seq, ATAC seq, mei-INTACT, meiMIGS, meiOE, mei-dCas9-Suntag/VP64 or SRDX, COmapper 등 새로운 연구 기법들을 활용하고 개발한다.
Meiosis is fundamental to sexual reproduction and produces genetic diversity in progeny. Meiotic recombination is initiated by programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) formation. The repair of DSBs leads to crossovers or non-crossovers via DSB repair. Despite the induction of excess DSBs, only a subset matures to crossovers. Anti-recombination factors restrict crossovers while interference causes even-spaced crossover patterns by preventing the coincidence of crossovers in the same chromosomes. The DSBs and crossovers are non-uniform along chromosomes, typically occurring at narrow regions, called recombination hotspots. Plant meiotic recombination hotspots occur at gene promoters and terminators in euchromatin while heterochromatin is suppressed, indicating that chromatin structure influences recombination distribution (Choi et. al., 2013
Nature genetics
, Choi et. al., 2018
Genome Research
). Notably, the meiotic recombination process requires dynamic assembly and disassembly of meiotic
protein complexes
in time and space.
We aim to understand
mechanistically
how meiotic recombination is controlled
by the interplay between meiotic proteins and the higher order of chromosome structure
. To achieve this, we apply advanced methods of recombination measurements at different scales from single base-pair to genome (
SPO11-oligonucleotide seq
(~bp),
pollen typing
(~10 kb),
fluorescent seed and pollen reporter systems
(~1-5 Mb),
genotyping-by-sequencing
(genome)). We have performed
a forward genetic screen of high crossover rate mutants (hcr1, hcr2, hcr3, hcr6 and hcr7) using high-throughput fluorescent seed-scoring and tetrad analysis in Arabidopsis and chracterized them
(
hcr3:Nature Plants
,
hcr2:EMBO J
,
hcr1:Nature Plants
).
We have also developed "
DeepTetrad
", a deep learning-based image recognition package for pollen tetrad analysis that enables high-throughput measurements of crossover frequency and interference in individual plants. In addition, we are intensively using the CRISPR/Cas9 system, which allows us to edit the genome and control gene expression for studying meiotic recombination in plants.
​
Our studies on meiotic recombination can help accelerate plant breeding for crop improvement by recombining or mapping useful genetic variations that occur spontaneously or as a result of mutagenesis in wild-type plant accessions at particular areas and diverse domesticated varieties. New combinations of DNA variations contributing to crop productivity, disease resistance, fruit, and grain quality can be generated by increasing crossover frequency between tightly linked alleles that had been hardly recombined along a chromosome. Once useful DNA variations are identified by genetic mapping by increasing crossovers, a CRISPR/Cas9 system can also be applied to edit plant genomes of elite varieties.
​

https://www.pgr.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 최규하 교수는 식물유전체재조합 연구실을 이끌며 모델 식물인 애기장대와 토마토를 대상으로 감수분열 중 상동염색체 간 교차(crossover)의 분자적 기전과 교차 간섭 현상을 연구하고 있습니다. 교차 빈도가 증가하는 돌연변이(hcr1, hcr2, hcr3, hcr6, hcr7)를 형광 종자·꽃가루 리포터(FTL) 기반 유전학적 스크리닝으로 발굴하고, 이를 유전체학·세포학·분자생물학 기법으로 특성 분석해 왔습니다. 연구 방법으로는 SPO11-oligo 시퀀싱, pollen typing, genotyping-by-sequencing, 면역세포학, CRISPR/Cas9 유전자 편집 등을 활용하며, 딥러닝 기반 꽃가루 사분자 분석 패키지 DeepTetrad와 롱리드 시퀀싱 기반 고해상도 교차 지도 작성법 COmapper를 개발했습니다. 주요 성과는 Nature Genetics, Nature Plants, PNAS, EMBO Journal, New Phytologist, Plant Cell 등에 발표되었으며, 교차 조절 연구를 통해 작물 개량과 육종 가속화에 기여하는 것을 목표로 합니다.

CHOI Laboratory Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine
We ask first-order questions that redefine how cells make decisions.
A long-term quest to decode principles of cell-niche communication and emergent tissue behavior.
Hot Issue
Regulation of Stem Cells during Regeneration, Repair, and Aging
Our lab focuses on understanding the biology of stem cells in the skin, particularly in the hair follicle and epidermis, and their interaction with the stem cell niche. We aim to uncover the mechanisms that regulate cell identity, tissue regeneration, aging, and organ development, using both in vivo models and organoid systems.

Lab Philosophy
"We prioritize questions over techniques."
"We value results that challenge our own models."
"We believe small perturbations can reveal governing principles of complex biological systems."
Research Overview
Classic regenerative biology focuses on stem cell behavior in isolation.
We ask instead:
When a subset of cells changes state, how does that perturb local niches, remodel tissue networks, and amplify regenerative responses?
Our recent work demonstrates that partial reprogramming can propagate widespread repair characteristics across cell types and environments.
Featured Publications
Nature Communications (2026)
We show that mosaic partial cellular reprogramming not only alters targeted epithelial cells but also remodels neighboring microenvironments and immune networks, leading to enhanced wound healing and tissue regeneration.
▪
Hair Follicle Stem Cells and Their Niches
we investigate the interaction between hair follicle stem cells and their niches
▪
Cellular Identity and In Vivo Reprogramming of Epidermal Cells
we investigate how epidermal cells can be reprogrammed and the underlying mechanisms
▪
Organoid
we investigate mechanisms of development and regeneration using organoids
▪
Aging
we investigate structural and functional changes of the skin with aging
▪
Tissue Regeneration
we investigate regeneration mechanisms by examining the interactions between stem cells and their niches during tissue regeneration

CHOI Laboratory Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine
We ask first-order questions that redefine how cells make decisions.
A long-term quest to decode principles of cell-niche communication and emergent tissue behavior.
Hot Issue
Regulation of Stem Cells during Regeneration, Repair, and Aging
Our lab focuses on understanding the biology of stem cells in the skin, particularly in the hair follicle and epidermis, and their interaction with the stem cell niche. We aim to uncover the mechanisms that regulate cell identity, tissue regeneration, aging, and organ development, using both in vivo models and organoid systems.

https://choilab.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 최세규 교수는 POSTECH 생명과학과 부교수이자 줄기세포생물학·재생의학 연구실(Lab of Stem Cell Biology and Regenerative Medicine)의 책임자로, 2021년 8월부터 2026년 8월까지 조교수로 재직한 뒤 2026년 9월 부교수로 승진했으며 POSTECH 의과학(Medical Science and Engineering) 겸직도 맡고 있습니다. 서강대 생명과학과 학사와 KAIST 생명과학과 박사를 거쳐 서울대 IMBG와 하버드대 줄기세포·재생생물학과(HSCI)에서 박사후연구원 및 연구원으로 일했습니다. 연구는 피부, 특히 모낭과 표피의 줄기세포와 줄기세포 니치의 상호작용에 초점을 두며, 세포 정체성 조절, 생체 내 리프로그래밍, 오가노이드, 노화, 조직 재생 기전을 생체 모델과 오가노이드 시스템으로 규명하고 있습니다. 대표 성과로 모자이크 부분 표피 리프로그래밍이 주변 세포와 니치, 면역 네트워크를 재편해 상처 치유와 조직 재생을 촉진함을 밝힌 Nature Communications(2026) 논문이 있으며, 이와 관련해 당뇨·고령 환자의 상처 회복을 돕는 피부 재생 원리 규명으로 언론에 보도되었습니다. 또한 2025년 보건복지부 첨단재생의료 유공 장관표창, 2025 BMB Reports Award, 2023 포스코청암재단 사이언스 펠로십을 받았고, 2026년 정해문신진유전학자상과 동천신진과학자상을 수상했으며 BMC Biology, Molecules and Cells, International Journal of Stem Cells 등의 편집위원으로 활동하고 있습니다.

RESEARCH | 조직 재생 및 발달 연구실
RESEARCH
다른메뉴보기
In the Laboratory of Tissue Regeneration and Development, we are dedicated to unraveling the intricate dynamics of
tissue repair and development
, employing
mouse skin and embryos
as our model systems. Our research initiatives delve into the complexities of
wound healing process
and the sophisticated landscape of
tissue development, including embryonic growth
.
At the core of our investigations lies a comprehensive exploration of the roles played by
stem cells
, emphasizing their intercellular communication within the tissue microenvironment, occurring in diverse forms, including
extracellular vesicles
. Navigating the elaborate system of cellular communication, differentiation, and regeneration, our objective is to elucidate the underlying mechanisms governing these processes. Ultimately, our goal is to provide innovative therapeutic strategies that advance regenerative medicine and effectively address tissue-related disorders.
Research Area
•Tissue repair and regeneration
-
Stem cell biology
-
Intercellular communication & Extracellular vesicles
-
Aging
•Tissue development
-
Embryonic development
-
Cellular senescence
Research topics
•Investigating the interaction between tissue-resident stem cells and their microenvironment during the process of skin wound healing.
•Exploring the roles played by intercellular communication via extracellular vesicles (i.e. microvesicles and exosomes) in the wound healing process.
•Studying the effects of aging-induced changes in stem cells on delayed wound healing.
•Unraveling the mechanisms and significance of intercellular communication during mammalian embryonic development.
•Understanding the contributions of cellular senescence to wound healing and embryonic development.
조직 재생 및 발달 연구실에서는 크게 다음과 같은 연구를 수행하고 있습니다.
•조직 재생 연구
조직이 손상되었을 때 조직의 치유와 재생에 대해 연구합니다. 조직 내의 성체 줄기세포가 어떠한 역할을 하는지에 집중하며, 특히 줄기세포와 주변 미세환경과의 상호작용이 조직 전반의 재생에 미치는 영향에 대해 알아봅니다. 마우스 피부 창상 모델을 이용하여 조직 재생 과정의 기전을 밝히고, 재생 의학적인 관점에서 창상 지연에 대한 새로운 접근법을 찾는 것을 목표로 합니다.
•조직 발달 연구
배아 발생 동안 조직 발달의 역학에 대해 연구합니다. 조직 발달 과정에서 줄기세포의 역할을 규명하고, 조직 발달에 영향을 미치는 다양한 인자들의 상호작용을 연구합니다. 마우스 배아를 모델로 하여 배아 내 세포 간 상호작용이 조직과 기관의 발달에 미치는 영향과 그 기전을 알아보고, 장기적으로는 발달 중 발생할 수 있는 질병의 치료 전략을 제시하고자 합니다.
주요 연구 주제는 다음과 같습니다.
•피부 창상 치유 과정에서 줄기세포와 주변 미세환경 사이의 상호작용 연구
•노화에 따른 성체 줄기세포의 변화와 이에 따른 창상 치유 지연 기전 연구
•포유류 배아 발생 중 세포 간 상호작용 기전과 그 역할 연구
•창상 치유 과정 동안 세포외소포체 (extracellular vesicle; microvesicle & exosome)를 통한 세포 간 정보 전달의 역할 연구
•창상 치유와 배아 발생 과정 동안 세포 노화 (cellular senescence)의 발생 기전과 역할 연구
학부생은 본 실험실 연구 참여
를 통해 위의 주제에 대해 연구하는 동안 생명과학 연구에 필요한 다양한 실험 기법을 배울 수 있습니다.
세포분자생물학 기법
- 조직/세포 형광 면역 염색 후 현미경 관찰 및 이미지 분석
- 세포배양
- Western blot, conventional PCR, qRT-PCR
- 바이러스 벡터와 리포솜을 이용한 세포 형질전환
마우스 실험 기법
- 마우스 핸들링 및 브리딩
- 조직 미세해부 (microdisection)
- 마우스 배아 해부 및 배아 전체 염색 (whole mount staining)
기타 실험 기법
- 유세포 분리 (FACS; Fluorescence-activated cell sorting)와 분석 (FACS analysis)
- H&E 염색 및 조직학적 분석
- 유전자 발현 조절을 알아보기 위한 시퀀싱 결과 분석

https://hurlab.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 허윤하 교수는 수의학 학사(서울대)와 코넬대 분자의학 박사 학위를 받은 뒤 록펠러대 Elaine Fuchs 연구실에서 AACR Immuno-Oncology 박사후연구원으로 일했고, 2024년 2월부터 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 생명과학과 조교수로 재직하며 조직 재생 및 발달 연구실(Laboratory of Tissue Regeneration & Development)을 이끌고 있습니다. 연구실은 마우스 피부와 배아를 모델로 창상 이후 조직의 치유·재생과 배아 발생 중 조직 발달의 역학을 다루며, 성체·표피 줄기세포와 주변 미세환경의 상호작용, 세포외소포체(미세소포·엑소좀)를 통한 세포 간 정보 전달, 노화 및 세포 노화(cellular senescence)의 역할을 주요 주제로 삼고 있습니다. 궁극적으로는 재생의학 관점에서 창상 치유 지연과 발달 관련 질환에 대한 새로운 치료 전략을 제시하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 대표 성과로는 배아줄기세포 유래 세포외소포체가 FAK 활성화를 통해 줄기세포성을 유지함을 보고한 Developmental Cell(2021) 논문, 조직 손상 복구 경로를 규명한 Cell(2023) 공동 제1저자 논문, 그리고 Journal of Biological Chemistry(2025) 공동 제1저자 논문 등이 있으며, Nature(2024) 공저 논문에도 참여했습니다. 수상 경력으로는 2025년 POSCO Science Fellowship과 2022~2024년 AACR-Incyte Immuno-oncology Postdoctoral Research Fellowship이 있습니다.

본문
전고체 배터리는 액체 전해질 대신 고체를 사용하는 차세대 배터리로, 화재 위험이 낮고 에너지를 더 많이 저장할 수 있는데요.
국내 연구팀이 기존보다 수십 배 두꺼운 양극을 사용하면서도, 안정적으로 작동하는 전고체 배터리 플랫폼을 구현하는데 성공했습니다.
화면 보시겠습니다.
산화물계 고체 전해질은 안정성은 뛰어나지만 리튬 이온의 전도도가 낮다는 한계가 있습니다.
이를 위해 에너지를 많이 담기 위해 양극을 두껍게 만들면 내부 저항이 급격히 커지는 문제가 있었습니다.
연구팀은 이 문제를 해결하기 위해, 고체 전해질 내부의 리튬 이온 이동 경로를 재설계했습니다.
기존 소재의 '규소'와 '인'을 게르마늄으로 바꿔, 리튬 이온이 이동할 수 있는 통로를 넓히는 동시에 촘촘하게 연결한 겁니다.
이를 통해 전도도가 5배 이상 향상됐다고 밝혔는데요.
이를 바탕으로 140㎛ 두께의 양극을 가진 '초고에너지밀도 전고체 전지'까지 구현했다고도 설명했습니다.
연구진의 설명 들어보시죠.
[강 병 우 / 포항공과대학교 신소재공학과 교수 : "두껍게 만들면 어쨌든 같은 활물질이 훨씬 더 많이 들어가 있겠죠. / 굉장히 두껍게 만들어도 전체적인 충전과 방전하는 속도라든지 에너지 밀도가 굉장히 잘 유지가 된다는 게 이번 연구의 중요한 결과라고 생각하시면 될 것 같습니다."]
연구진은 기술이 상용화가 된다면 동일한 크기의 배터리 팩에 훨씬 더 많은 에너지를 담을 수 있어
전기차 주행거리가 늘어나는 등 효과들을 기대해볼 수 있을 것으로 전망했습니다.
지금까지 사이언스 이슈 다 모아온 김은별이었습니다.

http://amee.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 강병우 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 신소재공학 분야 교수로, Advanced Materials for Energy & Environment(AMEE) 연구실을 이끌며 리튬이차전지 소재와 차세대 배터리를 연구하고 있습니다. 주요 연구 주제는 차세대 전지를 위한 산화물계 고체전해질, 고성능 리튬이온전지용 양극활물질 설계·합성·전기화학 반응 메커니즘 규명, 그리고 LiFePO4와 SiO 음극, 리튬-공기전지 등 친환경·저비용 소재 개발입니다. 연구실 공지에 따르면 2024년에는 공기 안정성과 리튬 젖음성이 뛰어난 가넷형 고체전해질 개발과 리튬-공기전지 관련 성과가 포스텍 뉴스 및 언론에 소개되었고, 2026년 6월 YTN 사이언스에서는 고체전해질 내 규소와 인을 게르마늄으로 치환해 이온 전도도를 5배 이상 높이고 140㎛ 두께 양극을 적용한 초고에너지밀도 전고체전지 플랫폼 구현이 보도되었습니다. 홈페이지에는 Journal of Materials Chemistry A, Nano-Micro Letters 등에 실린 공저 논문 70편과 Li-Fe-Ti-Mo 계열 고용량 양이온 무질서 산화물 관련 특허가 등재되어 있으며, 배출된 석·박사 동문들은 삼성SDI, 삼성전자, 한국기계연구원, 포스코홀딩스 등으로 진출했습니다.

SHORT BIOGRAPHY
Jong-Hoon Kang, a materials scientist, is a Senior Research Fellow at the Center for van der Waals Quantum Solids (vdWQS), Institute for Basic Science (IBS), and an Assistant Professor at Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH). Kang’s research covers thin film epitaxy and the precise synthesis of atomic-scale semiconductors and diverse quantum materials, such as low-dimensional materials, superconductors, semimetals, topological Weyl semimetals, and high-k dielectrics. His recent research interests include artificially designed van der Waals heterostructures tailored for next-generation electronics and quantum devices.
Jong-Hoon Kang received his B.S. and M.S. degrees from Seoul National University before earning Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2018, with a dissertation on atomic structure design in iron-based superconductors. He joined the faculty of the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at POSTECH in 2022, following a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Chicago, where he investigated the synthesis of transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayer films and the creation of 3D nano-structured films for optical metamaterials. Earlier in his career, he worked as a research scientist at Samsung Electronics and LG Chem, developing advanced semiconductor processes for memory, logic, and optoelectronic devices. More recently, he has been exploring the atomic-scale epitaxy of novel quantum materials and the engineering of precise van der Waals heteroepitaxy. In 2022, he established the Atomic-scale Epitaxy and Quantum Materials Laboratory (EQML) at POSTECH.
WELCOME TO EQML!
Our laboratory is dedicated to the interdisciplinary research of low-dimensional epitaxial thin films, nano-interface science, and the analysis of quantum phenomena to bridge fundamental materials physics with applied engineering. We strive to realize 'materials, properties, and functionalities on demand' by synthesizing atomic-scale heterostructures and hybrid quantum condensed matter. Beyond traditional semiconductors, our scope extends to topological materials and multi-dimensional van der Waals systems, enabling the precise control of crystal structures and defects at the atomic level. By integrating advanced growth techniques with nanoscale geometric designs, we explore unprecedented physical properties through atomic-resolution imaging and transport measurements. Ultimately, our goal is to develop next-generation platforms for information electronics, energy, and quantum science, including ultra-sensitive sensors and low-power quantum devices.
Our laboratory is a member of IBS Center for Van der Waals Quantum Solids and focuses on research into two-dimensional van der Waals material devices with chemical vapor deposition method, leading to the discovery of new materials and their properties into future information technology.
For more details, including our research, people, publications, facilities, and news, please visit the
IBS vdwqs homepage
.
We are actively seeking passionate individuals interested in epitaxial growth of two-dimensional materials via chemical vapor deposition. If you're interested in joining our team, please email professor Jong-Hoon Kang at [이메일]. Please kindly attach your CV and include a summary of your research interests.
We look forward to potentially collaborating with you on exciting scientific endeavors!

RESEARCH INTERESTS
Atomic-scale Semiconductors & Quantum Materials Synthesis (materials on demand)
Our research foundation lies in the precision synthesis of atomic-scale semiconductors and quantum materials. We explore a vast landscape of material systems, ranging from fundamental semiconductors and superconductors to complex ferromagnets, ferroelectrics, and semimetals. By utilizing advanced growth techniques, we aim to achieve high-quality crystalline structures and integrate them with high-k dielectrics. This broad material platform allows us to investigate intrinsic quantum properties and provides the essential building blocks for developing next-generation technologies.
Thin Film Epitaxy for Heterostructure Design of 2D van der Waals Materials (properties on demand)
We utilize advanced thin film epitaxy to engineer van der Waals heterostructures that go beyond naturally occurring materials. Our approach emphasizes in-situ engineering, employing both vertical stacking and lateral growth techniques to create pristine, contamination-free interfaces. Furthermore, we actively explore the field of "twistronics" by controlling the twist angle between layers to form in-situ twist structures and ex-situ moiré superlattices. This precise manipulation of lattice interactions enables us to engineer electronic band structures and uncover novel correlated physical phenomena.
Nano-integrated Device Fabrication towards Electronics & Optoelectronics (functionalities on demand)
The ultimate goal of our laboratory is to translate quantum material breakthroughs into tangible nano-integrated devices. We fabricate and characterize a wide array of functional devices, including neuromorphic and logic architectures for future electronics, as well as high-performance photodetectors for optoelectronics. Our research also extends to spintronics, exploiting magnetoelectric effects for low-power data processing, and quantum devices such as Josephson junctions, contributing to the advancement of quantum computing and information technologies.

https://eqml.postech.ac.kr.summary: 강종훈 교수는 POSTECH 신소재공학과 조교수이자 기초과학연구원(IBS) 반데르발스 양자물질 연구단(vdWQS)의 수석연구원이며, POSTECH 일범 석좌교수와 포스코청암재단 청암 사이언스 펠로우로도 활동하고 있습니다. 서울대학교에서 학사·석사를 마친 뒤 2018년 위스콘신대학교 매디슨에서 철계 초전도체의 원자구조 설계를 주제로 재료공학 박사학위를 받았고, 시카고대학교 박사후연구원 시기에는 전이금속 디칼코게나이드(TMD) 단일층 박막 합성과 광학 메타물질용 3차원 나노구조 박막을 연구했습니다. 이전에는 삼성전자와 LG화학에서 메모리·로직·광전소자용 반도체 공정을 개발한 산업계 경력도 있으며, 2022년 POSTECH 부임과 함께 원자단위 에피택시·양자물질 연구실(EQML)을 설립했습니다. 주요 연구 분야는 박막 에피택시와 원자 수준 반도체 및 저차원 물질, 초전도체, 반금속, 위상 바일 반금속, 고유전율 절연체 등 양자물질의 정밀 합성이며, 최근에는 차세대 전자·양자 소자를 위한 인공 반데르발스 이종구조와 화학기상증착 기반 2차원 소재 성장에 주력하고 있습니다. 학술 활동으로 ENGE 2026 조직위원회 재무위원장, ICMOVPE XXII 국제프로그램위원 등을 맡고 있고, POSTECH에서 우수강의상 등 교육 관련 수상과 제15회 포스코사이언스펠로십 선정 실적이 있습니다.

The Augmented Materials Design Laboratory develops advanced materials for sustainable energy and environmental technologies by leveraging atomistic simulations to uncover fundamental mechanisms and transform them into experimentally viable design strategies. We employ density functional theory (DFT), molecular dynamics (MD), and multiscale simulation approaches to rigorously elucidate reaction mechanisms and the origins of material properties at the atomic level. Based on these insights, our research focuses on the design of high-performance electrochemical catalyst materials for energy and environmental applications, including green hydrogen production, hydrogen storage, carbon dioxide reduction, and wastewater treatment. By bridging multiple spatial and temporal scales, we seek to achieve a deep understanding of atomic and molecular interactions under realistic reaction environments and to establish practical, reality-oriented materials design strategies that can be directly implemented in experiments. Such computation-driven design serves as a key tool for reducing trial-and-error processes and significantly accelerating the discovery and optimization of novel materials.
증강형 재료 설계 연구실은 원자단위 시뮬레이션을 통해 재료의 본질을 이해하고, 그 지식을 실험적으로 구현 가능한 설계 원리로 확장함으로써 지속가능 에너지 및 환경 기술을 선도하는 신소재를 개발합니다. 본 연구실은 범밀도 밀도범함수이론(DFT), 분자동역학(MD), 다중 스케일 시뮬레이션 기법을 활용하여 원자 수준에서의 반응 메커니즘과 물성의 기원을 정밀하게 규명하고, 이를 바탕으로 그린 수소 생산, 수소 저장, 이산화탄소 환원, 폐수 처리 등 에너지·환경 분야에 요구되는 고성능 전기화학 촉매 소재를 설계·제안합니다. 특히 서로 다른 공간 및 시간 스케일을 아우르는 시뮬레이션 접근을 통해, 실제 반응 환경에서 원자와 분자가 어떻게 상호작용하는지를 깊이 있게 이해하고, 실험적으로 구현 가능한 현실 지향적 소재 디자인 전략을 구축하는 데 주력합니다. 이러한 계산 기반 설계는 시행착오를 줄이고, 신소재 개발의 속도와 효율을 획기적으로 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

Reaction Mechanism & Kinetics
Multiscale Dynamics
Method Development
Application
Reaction Mechanism and Kinetics
To develop high-performance catalytic materials, it is essential to understand reaction mechanisms occurring on catalyst surfaces. Using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we can quantify the energetic requirements of chemical reactions, including reaction energies and activation barriers. From this information, we can further estimate reaction rates and kinetics.
These energetic and kinetic properties strongly depend on the nature of the catalyst and the surrounding reaction environment. By virtually tuning the identity of catalytic materials or modifying reaction conditions, we can systematically screen a wide range of candidate materials and identify promising catalysts that enhance the desired chemical reactions.
Grand canonical DFT calculations
Conventional density functional theory (DFT) calculations are typically limited to charge-neutral systems. In contrast, electrochemical reactions occur under an applied bias, where the number of electrons in the system continuously varies. As a result, standard DFT approaches cannot directly capture the effect of electrode potential on reaction energetics and kinetics. Grand canonical DFT (GC-DFT) overcomes this limitation by allowing the number of electrons to change at a fixed electrochemical potential, thereby accurately describing the charging behavior of electrochemical interfaces. This framework enables direct and quantitative comparisons between computed reaction energetics and kinetics and experimental electrochemical measurements. In our research, we employ grand canonical DFT to investigate potential-dependent reaction mechanisms and catalytic activity at electrified interfaces, providing realistic atomic-level insights into electrochemical processes under operating conditions.
Multiscale Dynamics
Multiscale molecular dynamics simulations enable us to track atomic trajectories in complex systems across a wide range of spatial and temporal scales. Depending on the length and time scales of interest, as well as the specific goals of the simulation, we employ different computational approaches. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) provides quantum-mechanical accuracy for the entire system, naturally allowing for the formation and cleavage of chemical bonds. However, AIMD is typically limited to systems containing a few hundred atoms and simulation times of less than 1 ns. In contrast, classical force-field-based molecular dynamics (MD) can be applied to systems comprising millions of atoms, reaching timescales up to microseconds. Through classical MD simulations, we can efficiently evaluate equilibrium structures of complex systems as well as mass transport properties, such as diffusion and ionic conductivity, under realistic conditions.

Method Development
Cyclic Voltammetry Simulation
Cyclic voltammetry (CV) is one of the most fundamental experimental techniques in electrochemistry, providing a direct current response to an applied potential. Despite its apparent simplicity, CV contains rich and invaluable information about electrochemical systems. In our research, we simulate CV curves using a bottom-up, atomistic approach based on the energetics of redox reactions occurring at electrode surfaces. This framework enables us to elucidate how surface intermediates evolve as a function of the applied potential. By directly comparing simulated CVs with experimental measurements, we can rigorously validate our theoretical models and gain mechanistic insight into electrochemical processes.
Hybrid QM/MM scheme
Hybrid Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) methods are well established in the field of biomolecular simulations. This approach partitions the entire system into two subsystems: a QM region, where a quantum-mechanical description is required (e.g., ligand binding sites in proteins), and an MM region, where chemical reactions do not occur and classical force fields are sufficient. In electrocatalytic systems, however, proton (H⁺) diffusion is strongly coupled with the solvent environment, involving frequent formation and cleavage of chemical bonds with surrounding water molecules. Such processes inherently require a QM-level description. This coupling complicates the application of conventional QM/MM methods, as the boundary between the QM and MM regions is neither fixed nor clearly defined, but instead changes dynamically due to proton hopping. To overcome this limitation, we have developed an adaptive boundary-shifting QM/MM method that enables real-time simulation of proton (and hydroxide) diffusion and their recombination in aqueous environments, where the solvation shells of H⁺ and OH⁻ continuously evolve. This approach naturally captures dynamic proton transfer processes while maintaining computational efficiency. Furthermore, the method can be extended to investigate other mass transport phenomena, such as lithium-ion diffusion in polymer electrolytes (e.g., Nafion).

Applications
Water Electrolysis
Green hydrogen is hydrogen gas produced by directly splitting the H–O bonds of water molecules using sustainable energy sources such as photovoltaic cells or wind turbines. However, in addition to the high cost of renewable electricity and the limited scale of current production, the reliance on expensive catalysts, such as iridium, makes it challenging to achieve the ultimate cost target of $1 per kg of H
2
. In our research, we have investigated the gold-standard IrO
2
catalyst through atomistic modeling to uncover its activity and stability at the atomic level. Based on these insights, we explore strategies to reduce iridium loading or partially substitute iridium with ruthenium, which is approximately ten times less expensive, while maintaining high catalytic performance.
Fuel Cell
Efficient utilization of hydrogen is a key requirement for building a sustainable energy society. In fuel cells, hydrogen is electrochemically converted into electricity and water, offering a clean and highly efficient energy conversion pathway. However, the performance and durability of fuel cells are strongly limited by sluggish electrode reactions at the anode and the use of costly platinum-based catalysts. Our research focuses on understanding electrode reaction mechanisms and we aim to design high-performance and cost-effective catalysts that enable efficient hydrogen utilization with reduced precious-metal content.
CO
2
Conversion
Electrochemical CO
2
conversion provides a promising route to transform carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals and fuels, such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and alcohols, using renewable electricity. Despite its potential, CO
2
reduction suffers from limited energy efficiency and low selectivity due to competing side reactions. Using first-principles calculations and molecular simulations, we investigate reaction pathways and catalyst–electrolyte interactions on catalytic surfaces. Our goal is to establish atomic-level design principles that enable selective and efficient CO
2
conversion, contributing to carbon-neutral energy cycles.

The Augmented Materials Design Laboratory at POSTECH (Principal Investigator: Prof. Soonho Kwon, [이메일]) is seeking graduate students (M.S./Ph.D.) and interns to join our team. Our research focuses on advancing the transition toward a sustainable society through computational materials science. We aim to understand complex systems from the atomic scale using simulations and to design novel materials with enhanced functionality. Our work spans a wide range of theoretical and computational approaches, from quantum-mechanical modeling of chemical reactions to large-scale simulations based on classical mechanics, as well as the development of new methodologies tailored to specific research challenges. We welcome applications from prospective M.S. and Ph.D. students, as well as undergraduate research interns. Students interested in our research, graduate programs, or individual consultations are encouraged to contact us at any time. Applicants from diverse academic backgrounds—including materials science, chemistry, chemical engineering, physics, and mechanical engineering—are strongly encouraged to apply.
POSTECH 증강형 재료 설계 연구실(지도교수: 권순호, [이메일])에서 대학원생 / 인턴을 모집합니다. 우리 연구실에서는 전산재료과학을 통해 지속가능사회로의 전환을 돕는 연구를 진행하고 있습니다. 시뮬레이션을 통해 시스템을 원자단위에서부터 이해하고 새로운 재료를 설계하는 연구를 지향하고 있으며, 양자역학을 이용한 화학반응부터 뉴턴역학을 이용한 대규모 시뮬레이션 및 연구목표에 맞는 필요한 새로운 방법론 개발 또한 진행하고 있습니다. 석·박사과정 및 학부 연구생들을 모집하오니 연구실의 다양한 정보와 대학원 진학 관련 궁금한 점이 있거나 상담을 원하는 학생들은 언제든지 연락주시기 바랍니다. 신소재/화학/화학공학/물리학/기계를 포함하여 다양한 학부 전공자들의 지원을 적극 장려합니다.

https://skwon.postech.ac.kr.summary: 권순호 교수는 POSTECH 증강형 재료 설계 연구실(Augmented Materials Design Lab)을 이끄는 책임교수로, 전산재료과학을 통해 지속가능 사회로의 전환에 기여하는 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 밀도범함수이론(DFT), 분자동역학(MD), 다중 스케일 시뮬레이션과 더불어 전극 전위를 직접 반영할 수 있는 그랜드 캐노니컬 DFT 기법을 활용해 원자 수준에서 반응 메커니즘과 물성의 기원을 규명하고, 이를 실험적으로 구현 가능한 소재 설계 전략으로 확장하는 데 주력합니다. 주요 응용 분야는 그린 수소 생산, 수소 저장, 이산화탄소 환원, 폐수 처리 등 에너지·환경용 고성능 전기화학 촉매 소재 설계이며, 연구 목적에 맞는 새로운 계산 방법론 개발도 함께 진행합니다. 대표 성과로는 동적 CO 전해 조건에서 CO2 생성을 거쳐 탄산염이 형성되며 구리 촉매가 피독될 수 있음을 이론적으로 규명한 Nature Catalysis 2026 논문의 공동 제1저자 연구가 있으며, 이 밖에도 CO2 환원, 산소 발생 반응, 수소 발생 반응 관련 논문을 다수 공동 저술했습니다. 교육 측면에서는 학부 과목 '재료의 기계적 성질'과 대학원 과목 '특론: 불균일 촉매 반응론'을 담당하고 있고, 석·박사과정생과 학부 연구인턴을 모집하고 있습니다.

Welcome Message
We are hiring!
The
Smart Soft Materials Lab
focuses on the study of hydrogels and the underlying polymers to develop novel functional materials. By strategically designing the types, compositions, and structures of polymers, the lab aims to create intelligent soft materials for various applications, including bio-inspired soft robots, energy devices, and drug delivery systems. The lab leverages the ability of polymers to undergo changes in response to external stimuli, utilizing these transformations in volume and shape to innovate efficient and functional materials.
스마트 소프트 재료 연구실(Smart Soft Materials Lab.)은 하이드로젤과 그에 기초한 고분자를 연구하여 새로운 기능성 재료를 개발하는 데 중점을 두고 있습니다. 고분자의 종류, 구성, 구조 등을 전략적으로 설계하여 지능형 연성 재료를 개발하고, 이를 생체 모방형 소프트 로봇, 에너지 소자, 약물 전달체 등 다양한 분야에 응용하고자 합니다. 외부 자극에 따른 고분자 사슬의 변화와 젤의 부피 및 형태 변화를 활용하여 효율적이고 혁신적인 재료를 연구하고 있습니다. 자세한 내용은
Research 탭
이나 교수님께서 출연하신
Youtube 링크
를 클릭하시기 바랍니다.

If you're interested in joining our team, please email
Youn Soo Kim
at
[이메일]
. Please kindly attach your CV and include a summary of your research interests.
★
Prospective graduate students are required to participate in research in our lab for at least one month during a vacation prior to admission.
We look forward to potentially collaborating with you on exciting scientific endeavors!

생체모방형 소프트 액추에이터 개발
액추에이터란 외부로부터 가해진 물리적, 화학적, 열 에너지 등을 제어 가능한 기계적인 운동으로 변환시키는 재료를 뜻합니다. 특히 재료 자체가 유연하여 부드러운 움직임을 재현할 수 있는 소프트 액추에이터의 연구가 최근에 활발히 진행되고 있습니다. 그 중에서도 하이드로젤 액추에이터는 유연한 고분자 사슬과 물로 구성 되었다는 재료의 특성 때문에 인체 근육과 비슷한 탄성과 강도를 갖고 있으며 생물체의 부드럽고 유연한 운동을 재현할 수 있기 때문에 생체 모방 액추에이터로서의 응용 가능성이 매우 높습니다. 보다 효율적이고 지능적인 액추에이터를 개발하기위해, 자연 및 생물학적 시스템에서 찾을 수 있는 움직임에 대한 기본 구동 메커니즘을 이해하는 것이 중요합니다. 본 연구실에서는 자극 응답성 고분자 젤의 합성과 분석을 바탕으로 외부자극에 의해 큰 부피 변화와 빠른 변형을 발생시킬 수 있는 젤 액추에이터 개발을 진행하고 있습니다.

생명체 내부의 고분자 네트워크는 형태 유지, 신호 전달, 기계적 자극 반응 등 생명 유지에 핵심적인 역할을 합니다. 액틴, 콜라겐, 뮤신 등은 정교한 서열에 따라 자기조립하여 안정적인 3차원 구조를 형성하며, 높은 탄성, 신장성, 자가 치유 등의 특성을 나타냅니다. 이러한 생체 네트워크를 모방한 합성 고분자 시스템이 활발히 연구되고 있지만, 서열 제어의 어려움으로 인해 구조적 정밀성과 기능 구현에 한계가 있습니다. 본 연구에서는 RAFT 중합법을 이용한 one-pot 합성을 통해 서열이 정밀하게 조절된 다중 블록 공중합체를 제작하고 있습니다. RAFT 중합은 각 블록의 길이, 조성, 배열 순서를 제어할 수 있어, 이온성 블록을 정밀하게 설계하고, 반대 전하 간의 전기적 인력을 이용해 고도로 정렬된 자기조립 네트워크를 형성할 수 있습니다. 이 과정에서 새로운 자기조립 단위인 '네트머(netmer)'를 발견하였습니다. 네트머는 코어와 브릿지가 반복되는 네트워크 구조로, 루프 형성이 억제되고 결합력이 향상된 특징을 가집니다. RAFT 기반 서열 제어를 통해 네트머의 구조적 특성을 조절할 수 있으며, 이를 바탕으로 형성된 하이드로젤은 기존 마이셀 기반 하이드로젤에 비해 저장탄성률이 11.5배, 연신율이 3배 향상되었습니다. 또한 우수한 자가 치유 성능과 반복 하중에 대한 내구성도 확인하였습니다. 이러한 결과는 서열 제어 고분자와 자기조립 원리를 융합한 새로운 하이드로겔 설계 전략으로, 다양한 기능성 소재 개발에 적용될 수 있습니다.

겔 고분자 전해질 개발
차세대 전해질 소재로 주목받고 있는 겔 고분자 전해질은 기존 분리막 기반 전해질이 가지는 복잡한 공정과 제한된 온도 안정성의 한계를 극복할 수 있는 대안으로 떠오르고 있습니다. 본 연구실에서는 개시제, 가열, 가교제가 필요 없는 자가중합 기반의 젤 전해질을 개발하고 있으며, 상온에서 간단히 제조 가능하면서도 균일한 젤 구조를 형성하여 안정적인 전기화학적 성능을 확보할 수 있습니다. 또한, –30°C 저온부터 125°C 고온까지 극한 온도 환경에서도 기계적 안정성과 이온전도성을 유지할 수 있는 젤 전해질 시스템을 개발하고 있습니다. 본 연구는 단순화된 공정과 우수한 온도 내구성을 바탕으로 웨어러블 소자, 극한 환경용 에너지 저장 시스템 등에 활용될 수 있는 범용성 높은 젤 전해질 기술을 제공하는 것을 목표로 하고 있습니다.

증발하지 않는 차세대 젤 연구
젤 소재는 높은 수분 함량과 유연성 덕분에 다양한 응용이 가능하지만, 장시간 사용 시 수분 증발로 인한 성능 저하가 큰 문제로 작용해 왔습니다. 본 연구실에서는 이러한 한계를 극복하기 위해 증발하지 않는 젤 시스템을 개발하고 있으며, 젤의 내부 및 표면 구조를 미세하게 제어함으로써 물리적·화학적 안정성을 향상시키고자 합니다. 특히, 다양한 기질 위에 장기간 접착 가능한 비증발 접착 젤과 기계적 강도 조절이 가능한 비증발 터프 젤을 구현함으로써, 젤의 표면 특성과 내부 네트워크 구조를 정밀하게 설계하고 있습니다. 이로 인해 유리, 금속, 고무, 피부 등 다양한 환경에서도 지속적인 부착력이 유지되며, 기계적 내구성 또한 사용자 요구에 맞춰 조절이 가능합니다. 본 연구는 장기간 안정성이 요구되는 생체부착소재, 소프트 로보틱스, 스마트 센서 등 다양한 응용 분야에서 핵심적인 역할을 할 수 있는 차세대 고기능 젤 플랫폼을 제시합니다.

http://hydrogel.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 김연수(Youn Soo Kim) 교수는 POSTECH에 소속되어 스마트 소프트 재료 연구실(Smart Soft Materials Lab.)을 이끌고 있습니다. 연구실은 하이드로젤과 그 기반 고분자의 종류·조성·구조를 전략적으로 설계해 새로운 기능성 연성 재료를 개발하며, 생체모방형 소프트 액추에이터, 전기전도성 하이드로젤, 젤 고분자 전해질, 비휘발성 젤 등을 주요 연구 주제로 다루고 있습니다. 외부 자극에 반응하는 고분자 사슬 변화와 젤의 부피·형태 변화를 활용해 생체모방 소프트 로봇, 에너지 소자, 약물 전달체 등으로의 응용을 목표로 합니다. 대표 성과로는 교신저자로 참여한 유연 슈퍼커패시터용 상분리 P(HEA-co-MMA)/라포나이트/LiCl 부동 나노복합 하이드로젤 전해질 논문(Chemical Engineering Journal, 2026)이 있으며, 상온에서 개시제·가교제 없이 자가중합되는 하이드로젤 전해질 연구(Small, 2026)도 연구실의 주요 이슈로 소개되어 있습니다. 또한 자려진동 젤 액추에이터를 다룬 일본어 단행본 장(소프트액추에이터의 재료·구성·응용기술, S&T출판, 2016)의 공저자로 참여했습니다.

Fuel Cell
A fuel cell uses the chemical energy of hydrogen or another fuel to cleanly and efficiently produce electricity. If hydrogen is the fuel, electricity, water, and heat are the only products. Fuel cells are unique in terms of the variety of their potential applications; they can provide power for systems as large as a utility power station and as small as a laptop computer. Fuel cells can operate at higher efficiencies than combustion engines, and can convert the chemical energy in the fuel to electrical energy with efficiencies of up to 60%. Fuel cells have lower emissions than combustion engines. Hydrogen fuel cells emit only water, so there are no carbon dioxide emissions and no air pollutants that create smog and cause health problems at the point of operation. Also, fuel cells are quiet during operation as they have fewer moving parts.
Battery
Recent development of Electrical vehicles, and portable devices requires high capacity and energy density batteries. Many other researches were conducted to develop electrical performance of the batteries. Such as doping, electrode surface modification and etc. However closer research in atomic and electronic scale research was barely accomplished. Our group closely investigate the structural or electrical phenomenon, utilizing PLS(Pohang Light Source). We expect this research will provide fundamental understanding of battery performance in atomic scale and further development of high capacity and energy density energy.
Water Electrolysis
Water electrolysis(also called water splitting) is the decomposition of water into oxygen and hydrogen gas due to the passage of an electric current. This technique can be used to make hydrogen gas, a main component of hydrogen fuel, and breathable oxygen gas. It ideally requires a potential difference of 1.23 V to split water. However, real water electrolyzers require higher voltages for the reaction to proceed. The part that exceeds 1.23 V is called overpotential, and represents any kind of loss and nonideality in the electrochemical process. Electrocatalysts can facilitate this reaction.
CO2 Reduction
Carbon dioxide is an abundant potential carbon resource on Earth, and it is also a greenhouse gas whose atmospheric concentration has increased sharply over the past two centuries Chemical fixation of carbon dioxide (CO2) is an attractive technique for utilization of carbon resources, as well as for the reduction of the atmospheric concentration of CO2. Carbon dioxide is a potential carbon resource abundant on earth. The electrochemical reduction of CO2 is the conversion of carbon dioxide to more reduced chemical species. The first examples of electrochemical reduction of carbon dioxide are from the 19th century, when carbon dioxide was reduced to carbon monoxide using a zinc cathode. Research in this field intensified in the 1980s following the oil embargoes of the 1970s. CO2 can be removed by the reduction that produces various chemicals, such as carbon monoxide (CO), methanol (CH3OH), methane (CH4), and formic acid (HCOOH). In our lab, we are mainly focused on the CO2 reduction to CO using various metallic catalysts.
Anti-corrosion
In modern times, with the development of stainless steel, the corrosion resistance of steel has improved dramatically. However, corrosion in extreme conditions such as cryogenic, high temperatures, abrasion and seawater environments still causes economical loss and environmental damage and has become a major cause of safety issues. Since it is almost impossible to replace and repair corrosion parts in such a harsh environment, the need for structural materials with strong corrosion resistance is increasing day by day. Our group is exploring ways to improve the anti-corrosion properties of structural materials without losing mechanical properties via alloy composition control or surface treatment.
Battery Recycling
In order to meet global target of carbon emission, automotive industries are radically changing. Millions of electric vehicles are now on roads, consequently, tones of end-of-life batteries will come out after decades. In comparison to the number of end-of-life batteries and market size of battery recycling industries in the near future, the development of technology is still lag behind and the players in this field are not enough. Thus, our group set our sight on developing advanced battery recycling technology using hydrometallurgical processes. Battery recycling technology definitely will occupy highly demanding part in battery industries.

http://lemp.postech.ac.kr.summary: 김용태 교수는 포스텍(POSTECH) 신소재공학 분야 교수로, 전극물성연구실(LEMP, Laboratory for Electrode Material Property)을 이끌고 있습니다. 서강대학교 화학공학과에서 학사(2000)와 석사(2002) 학위를 받은 뒤 일본 JAIST 재료과학 전공에서 박사학위(2006)를 취득했으며, 부산대 산업대학원 부원장(2010~2012)과 미국 Argonne National Laboratory 방문교수(2012~2013)를 거쳤습니다. 학회·학술 활동으로는 Journal of Mechanical Science and Technology 부편집장 및 Business Director, 한국전기화학회와 한국XAFS학회 총무이사, ECS PEFC 심포지엄 한국 대표 오거나이저 등을 맡고 있습니다. 연구 분야는 연료전지, 이차전지, 수전해, CO2 환원, 내식성 소재, 배터리 리사이클링 등 전극 소재와 전기화학 전반이며, 홈페이지에는 183편의 논문과 43건의 등록 특허, 95건의 출원 특허가 등재되어 있습니다. 또한 과학기술정보통신부의 대규모 수소 국제공동연구(H2GATHER) 사업에 최종 선정된 포스텍 컨소시엄에 참여하고 있으며, 학부 '에너지소재'와 대학원 '신소재공학특론: 소재 전기화학' 과목을 강의하고 있습니다.

that enable molecular recognition, enzyme catalysis, molecular transport, ion channeling, and even nanomechanical motions.

Research
Synergy of Science with Engineering
​
Science
and
engineering
are not separate but interact with each other. Intriguing scientific questions trigger methodological advances, and the advancement in technology stimulates another scientific curiosity. Within this reciprocal interaction,
Materials Science and Engineering has advanced and integrated them based on many novel materials.
Our lab is strongly interested in creating
novel
macr
o- and biomolecular materials that perform "protein-like" or "cell-like" molecular functions
, and we also develop
innovative techniques in addressing life-related fundamental questions
.
Pioneering Proteomimetics and Cytomimetics
To maintain a life, biological cells have incredible capabilities--
1)
replication/transmission/replacement of genetic information,
2)
catalyzing enzymatic reactions,
3)
recognition of molecular targets, and
4)
even regulation of molecule transport into and out of the cells. When looking into this amazing world, it is discovered that “
sequence-defined biopolymers
”, including nucleic acids (DNAs and RNAs), amino acids (proteins), and saccharides (carbohydrates), are the core elements of the living cells. Depending on the specific sequence of the biopolymers, they fold into unique 3D nanostructures that control a cellular life, and this is one of the essential principles in MOLECULAR BIOLOGY. Based on the fundamental principle, we intend to create highly ‘sequence-controlled’ biopolymers capable of performing valuable molecular functions, using innovative technologies: rational design and Darwinian evolution. With the newly developed molecular materials, we challenge not only the traditional fields of biotechnology such as the development of
high-performance biosensors
and
highly effective therapeutic agents
, but also creative and innovative ventures such as implementing
artificial cells
via sophisticated control of cellular functions, for which emerging SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY is aiming.
1. Molecular recognition reagent to control a life
Similar with monoclonal antibodies, nucleic acid-based aptamers possess the unique capability to recognize and bind specific target molecules. To date, it has been successfully proven that they can target a broad range of molecules, including proteins, small molecules, metal ions, whole cells, and even viruses, so that these synthetic biopolymers have been widely used for medical applications, such as
molecular diagnostics
and
targeted drug delivery
. Based on the innovative "
in vitro
selection technology," the target-specific aptamers can be readily created; we can selectively isolate them from 10E15-10E16 random sequences through the itinerary process of selection and amplification. The ability of the aptamers is not only limited to molecular recognition. Beyond target binding, they have amazing potential to control a life by modulating cellular signaling pathways. In our laboratory, we are conducting creative studies to control cellular signaling by developing artificial receptor regulators such as synthetic growth factors.
hACE2 mimicking for SARS-CoV-2 neutralization with exceptional binding tolerance to all kinds of mutants (Science Advances 2022)
2. Synthetic enzyme as a selective catalyst
The ability of enzymes is striking. They can precisely catalyze thousands of biological processes, from simple molecular synthesis to intricate neurotransmission. Natural enzymes, however, are specialized only for the specific functions required by living organisms, so changing their predetermined behaviors to a desired usage is exceptionally challenging. It is also unfortunate that the production of enzymes largely depends on biological synthesis which severely hampers mass production of high purity enzymes. Facing these issues, our group is developing ‘
synthetic enzymes
’ that mimic the efficient enzymatic system: an enzyme selectively recognizes its substrate and creates an optimal structure between the substrate and its active site which later results in a catalytic activity. To generate such synthetic enzymes, not only they are required to be structurally defined and chemically synthesized with a simple purification procedure, but also they should be able to selectively promote specific catalytic reactions like biological enzymes. Great examples of our synthetic enzymes are chemically-synthesizable nucleozymes. We previously reported several DNA/RNA enzymes (DNAzyme/ribozyme) capable of performing intriguing catalytic activities (
e.g.
, gene cleavage/ligation and peroxidation) via systematically mimicking enzymes’ modular structure. They are highly valuable in various applications; for example, target-specific catalysis can be used to construct
high-performance biosensors
, and as a genetic circuit, the nucleozymes can be installed into an artificial organism for the regulation of gene expression and protein production.
Peroxidase mimicking for ultra-fast oxidation of chromogetic substrates in complex environments (iScience 2022)
3. Nanomechanical motion-based molecular machine
In addition to target-specific binding and specific catalytic reaction, the sequence-controlled biopolymers can be programmed to conduct nanomechanical motions in response to their environmental changes. Our group is exploring nucleic acid-based molecular machines, in particular, “structure-switching aptamers” that can carry out target binding-induced mechanical motions. Because these molecular machines are composed of naturally-occurring nucleic acids, we can easily insert them into the genome of living organisms. For instance, RNA molecular machines embedded in messenger RNAs can serve as a
riboswitch that regulates the gene expression
by changing its molecular structure upon abrupt change in the target concentration. With the development of various RNA switches that respond to their corresponding targets, we can ultimately create
an artificial cell
capable of performing sophisticated functions in a programmed manner. This artificial cell is anticipated to be actively employed for industrial and military purposes as a high-yield microorganism that produces valuable molecules or a living biosensor that survives in field without power supply.
Creation of artificial cells with riboswitches of gene regulation (Biotechnology Advances 2019)
4. Target-selective molecular filtration membrane
Cell membrane, which is an essential component for cellular survival, regulates the transport of various molecules and ions through its own channels,
i.e.
, membrane proteins. Among them, ion channels play a crucial role in controlling physiological functions, such as electrical signal generation, neurotransmitter secretion, and cellular homeostasis, by selectively transporting ions into and out of the cell. Mimicking these natural ion channels, we are creating an unprecedented platform of selective molecular filtration membranes based on molecular recognition. Through our rational design and chemical synthesis of sequence-controlled biopolymers, we can generate
artificial molecular channels
to build synthetic membranes with selective permeability. When these ion-selective membranes are combined with next-generation ionic devices, the integrated system has great potential to be developed into an innovative biosensor capable of detecting cellular signals in real-time. The selective molecular channels can also be incorporated into liposomes and proteinosomes, and be further developed into a novel therapeutic system with controllable drug release ability.
Potassium ion-selective ion channel mimicking based on ab initio calculation (Nucleic Acids Research 2021)

https://ssohlab.weebly.com/.summary: 오승수 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 신소재공학과 부교수로, 화학공학과·융합생명공학부(i-bio)·환경공학부 겸직교수이며 연세대 융합기술연구소 겸직교수도 맡고 있습니다. 서울대학교에서 재료공학 학사와 석사를 마친 뒤 University of California, Santa Barbara에서 핵산 소재의 유도진화 기법을 주제로 박사학위를 받았고, 이후 UCSB와 하버드 의과대학(Jack W. Szostak 교수 연구실) 등에서 박사후연구원으로 근무했습니다. 그가 이끄는 Bio-molecular Materials Lab은 DNA/RNA, 아미노산 등 서열 제어가 가능한 생체고분자의 3차원 나노구조를 기반으로 분자 인식, 효소 촉매, 분자 수송, 이온 채널링 기능을 구현하는 프로테오미메틱스와 사이토미메틱스 분야를 개척하고, 고성능 바이오센서·치료제 및 인공세포 구현을 목표로 합니다. 대표 연구로는 앱타머 기반 SARS-CoV-2 전변이 전기화학 검출, 비조작 단백질에 대한 선택적 접합 기술(JACS), 이온성 액체로 안정화한 핵산의 분자 인식 등이 있으며, 관련 성과를 Journal of the American Chemical Society, Nucleic Acids Research, ACS Nano, Biosensors and Bioelectronics 등에 발표했습니다. 또한 BioChip Letters 편집장, BioChip Journal 부편집장, Macromolecular Research 편집위원으로 활동하고 있습니다.

Computational Nano-Materials Design Laboratory
전산나노소재 연구실에서는 물리, 화학적 원리를 기반으로 재료의 물성을 파악하고, 예측된 물성을 이용해서 신소재들을 다양한 에너지 기술에 맞게 최적화하는 작업을 수행합니다. 이는 분자동역학, 모델 헤밀토니언, 범밀도 함수 이론, 다체 제일원리 이론 등과 같은 다양한 컴퓨터 기반의 테크닉을 이용해서 진행됩니다. 또한, 기계학습 기반 멀티스케일 시뮬레이션 프레임을 이용하여 빠른 시간내에 신소재를 개발, 다양한 응용분야에 맞게 최적화하는 기술 개발도 수행하고 있습니다. 현재 이러한 연구에 관심있는 열정있는 대학원생, 박사후연구원을 모집중입니다. 연구참여와 관련한 정보는 Participation 탭을 통해 확인하시기 바랍니다. 관심있는 학생들의 많은 지원 부탁드립니다.

Big-data collection
N
LP based database generation from scientific document
As the interest in machine learning increases, the interest in databases for use in machine learning is also increasing. Despite the increasing demand for databases in the material field, there is no clear database to date. Therefore, in this project, we intend to build a database based on research results in the field of materials existing in Internet documents through natural language processing techniques.
Machine learning application
A
ssessing Additive Compositions for Glass Using MLP, MD, and DFT-based Simulations
Amorphous silicon dioxide (SiO₂) is a fundamental oxide material with extensive scientific and commercial applications, attributed to its excellent thermal properties, dielectric characteristics, and optical transmission performance. To enhance the transparency of silica glass—the amorphous form of SiO₂—dopants such as germanium (Ge) or titanium (Ti) are often introduced to increase optical light transmission. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, potential datasets are generated on Ge- and Ti-doped amorphous SiO₂ to train machine learning potentials. These trained models enable the reproduction of amorphous structures with quantum-level accuracy. The dielectric constant, and consequently the refractive index, of the Ge/Ti-doped amorphous SiO₂ is then calculated to assess the system’s transmission coefficient.
F
ull-Cycle AI Technology for Developing Ferroelectrics toward In-Memory Computing
In-memory computing (IMC) is a computing technology that performs data storage and computation within the system’s main memory, overcoming the von Neumann bottleneck. The IMC systems require superior memory devices with both scalable, non-volatile storage and low-power, high-endurance, high-speed computing properties. Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM) is a promising device for IMC systems, which is non-volatile and low power operation, but its large cell-size and weak endurance are still in challenges. A full-cycle AI-based materials design integrates materials, process, microstructure, device, and circuit level properties through AI-driven generation, prediction, and optimization. Using an automated data crawling system based on natural language processing (NLP) with experimental validation process, this design system can rapidly predict optimal recipes for superior FeRAM devices, addressing the shortcomings in current IMC applications.
U
nderstanding the domain walls movement of ferroelectric HfO2 with machine learning potential
HfO2-based FeRAM has been spotlighted as a key material for future semiconductor technologies such as logic-in-memory, neuromorphic computing, and negative capacitance FET, but it is facing difficulties in practical use due to its high coercive field and low domain wall velocity. Therefore, this study aims to understand and investigate the phenomenon related to the movement of domain walls under the electric field of HfO2-based ferroelectric materials at the atomic level through machine learning and molecular dynamics simulation.
A
ccelerated materials design of protonic ceramic electrolysis cell (PCEC) using first-principles calculation and machine learning
Protonic ceramic electrolysis cell is a next-generation hydrogen production system that can be operated at low temperatures and generates pure hydrogen from the fuel electrode. High chemical stability and proton conductivity material design is required as air electrode and electrolyte materials for PCEC. Using first-principle calculations, the mechanisms of proton conduction and water splitting reactions are identified, and doping materials are explored. Based on the first principle calculation data, PCEC materials are optimized in a wide composition space through a material performance prediction machine learning model.
D
iscovery of organic cathode material for high performance organic Li-ion battery
Inorganic cathode materials that are currently commercialized have environmental problems such as large amount of carbon emissions generated during the process and the use of expensive metals such as Co and Ni. Due to these problems, interest in organic-based batteries is increasing. However, in order to use organic-based cathode materials, low power, low energy density problems must be solved. Unlike inorganic materials, organic-based cathode materials have numerous possible combinations, so it is difficult to develop them through experiments. Therefore, we want to search for organic cathode materials with optimal performance through screening based on first-principle calculation and machine learning.
AI
based supercritical materials research
As global issues emerge, exploration and development of resources and energy in extreme environments such as space, deep sea, and polar regions are actively progressing. Supercritical materials that greatly exceed the physical properties of existing materials are indispensable for stable work. However, its slow development speed and high probability of failure are blocked the progressing. Therefore, in this project, 7 promising supercritical materials that are used in the future extreme environment were selected, and an AI platform that integrates material design/manufacturing, synthesis/analysis, and evaluation is built to develop those materials in a relatively short time.
P
rediction of polymer properties using machine learning from the composition of various raw materials
Various properties of copolymer generally come from their constituent units (monomer). Several factors including type of units, composition of units, manufacturing conditions can affect properties of copolymer. Traditionally, to achieve desired properties, trial-and-error experiment method have been used but the cost is high because a lot of samples to be prepared to test. In this project, to address the limitations, we predict properties of copolymer through the machine learning models. Experimental dataset comprised of over 350 features is used for training data. Based on the models, we aim to find out suitable materials and their optimized compositions for desired products.
Completed projects
D
evelopment of Novel Resistance Switching Materials by using First Principle-based Machine Learning Platform
AIM-HS(Ab Initio calculation based Machine learning High-throughput Screening) platform is Ab initio calculation high-throughput screening system based on multi-dimensional machine learning analysis. This project is purposed to detect hidden correlation between calculated properties and make criterion based on big data of Ab initio calculation. The final goal is material designing based on needs for material property.
D
evelopment of machine learning model for predicting corrosion of high corrosion-resistant alloy plated steel
Alloy plating is used to prevent corrosion of steel construction materials, but it has limited lifespan under harsh environments. Through a machine learning model developed from alloy plated steel corrosion images and experimental environment data, we predict lifespan of construction materials in real marine and soil environments.

I
dentification of Degradation Mechanisms in Ni-Based Cermet Cathodes in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOECs) via First-Principles Calculations
The Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cell (SOEC) is a promising technology for hydrogen production due to its use of a solid oxide electrolyte, which addresses compatibility and safety concerns typically associated with other systems. Operating at elevated temperatures, SOECs not only enhance hydrogen production efficiency but also provide thermal energy that can be leveraged for additional applications. Despite these advantages, SOEC stability remains a challenge, primarily due to the degradation of the Ni-based cermet cathode. High temperatures, steam concentrations, and applied voltages cause Ni within the cermet to aggregate and volatilize, yet the precise mechanisms underlying this degradation are not fully understood. To address this gap, first-principles calculations are employed to investigate the degradation processes in Ni cermet, with a focus on its surfaces and interfaces. This multi-scale analysis aims to elucidate various descriptors related to Ni cermet degradation, contributing valuable insights for the design of more stable Ni-based SOEC cathodes.

I
dentification of the mechanism of formation of Ni-rich NCM cathode material from Li raw materials
The sintering process of Ni-rich NCM cathode takes a long time. To identify the mechanism process of formation of Ni-rich NCM cathode by using the first principle calculation at the atomic level. Then, to derive reducing process time or improving quality based on the identified mechanism process.
D
opants Effect on the Stability of Ni-rich Li Cathodes
Ni-rich cathodes have been considered as promising cathode due to their high electrochemical capacities and low costs. However, the undesirable capacity fading hinders their development. We used first-principles calculations to understand physical origin of structural instability under low Li content and find dopants that can enhance stability.

esign and synthesis of novel Pb-free light-absorbers
Designing and tuning the crystal structure of the energy bands using first-principles calculation. Non- perovskite structure of the series Pb-free synthetic photoactive material New photoactive material development from photoelectric conversion efficiency and degradation characteristic
D
evelopment and Characterization of oxygen transport membrane (OTM) materials
Design new OTM(oxygen transport membrane) materials with high ionic and electronic conductivity. Understand the activation energy of oxygen ion diffusion inside OTM and the mechanism of redox reaction on OTM surface using first-principles calculation.

evelopment and Characterization of SOFC Component Materials
The unit cell configuration of equilibrium physical factors and chemical properties and optimizing the stack components through an electrochemical analysis of water in the drive condition.

전산나노소재 연구실
Hot Issue
Computational Nano-Materials Design Laboratory
전산나노소재 연구실에서는 물리, 화학적 원리를 기반으로 재료의 물성을 파악하고, 예측된 물성을 이용해서 신소재들을 다양한 에너지 기술에 맞게 최적화하는 작업을 수행합니다. 이는 분자동역학, 모델 헤밀토니언, 범밀도 함수 이론, 다체 제일원리 이론 등과 같은 다양한 컴퓨터 기반의 테크닉을 이용해서 진행됩니다. 또한, 기계학습 기반 멀티스케일 시뮬레이션 프레임을 이용하여 빠른 시간내에 신소재를 개발, 다양한 응용분야에 맞게 최적화하는 기술 개발도 수행하고 있습니다. 현재 이러한 연구에 관심있는 열정있는 대학원생, 박사후연구원을 모집중입니다. 연구참여와 관련한 정보는 Participation 탭을 통해 확인하시기 바랍니다. 관심있는 학생들의 많은 지원 부탁드립니다.

기본 연구참여는 5주간 진행되며, 먼저 4주에 걸쳐 밀도범함수이론 (DFT, density functional theory) 기반의 컴퓨터 계산을 통해 물질의 특성 (energetic stability, mechanical property, electronic structure, magnetic property, defect structure, ionic conductivity 등) 을 예측하는 방법을 배웁니다. DFT 계산은 VASP (Vienna Ab-initio Simulation Package) 소프트웨어와 고성능 컴퓨터를 이용합니다. 5주차에는 기계학습의 기초와 더불어 딥러닝을 통해 다양한 소재의 물성을 예측하는 과정에 대해 배웁니다. 5주간의 연습기간이 끝나면 그룹에서 진행중인 여러 응용 분야 (구조재료, 에너지, 바이오, 반도체) 중 원하는 특정 분야에 대해 DFT, 기계학습 등을 활용하여 물성을 예측하고 신소재를 개발하는 과제에 참여할 수 있습니다.

http://cnmd.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 이동화 교수는 POSTECH 신소재공학과, 첨단재료과학부 및 인공지능대학원 소속 부교수로, 전산나노소재 연구실(Computational Nano-Materials Design Laboratory)을 이끌고 있습니다. 미국 플로리다대학교에서 재료공학 석사(2007)와 박사(2010)를 받은 뒤 로렌스리버모어 국립연구소와 오크리지 국립연구소에서 박사후연구원을 지냈고, 전남대학교 조교수(2015~2017)를 거쳐 2017년 POSTECH에 부임해 2020년부터 부교수로 재직 중입니다. 연구실에서는 분자동역학, 범밀도함수이론(DFT), 모델 해밀토니언, 다체 제일원리 계산 등 전산 기법과 기계학습 기반 멀티스케일 시뮬레이션을 결합해 재료 물성을 예측하고 에너지·구조·전자·바이오 등 응용 분야에 맞는 신소재를 설계하는 연구를 수행합니다. 세부 과제로는 생성형 AI를 활용한 신소재 탐색, 자연어 처리 기반의 과학문헌 소재 데이터베이스 구축, 기계학습 퍼텐셜을 이용한 Ge/Ti 도핑 비정질 SiO2의 유전율·굴절률 예측, 촉매 반응의 전산 예측 등이 있습니다. 또한 저항변화 메모리 소재, 고엔트로피 합금, 베이지안 추론 기반 소재 역설계, 자연어처리 기반 소재 데이터베이스 관련 다수의 특허와 소프트웨어 등록을 보유하고 있으며, 대학원 강의 '전자구조계산학 개론'과 학부 강의 '소재수치해석'을 담당하고 있습니다.

What we are doing in the CMSE Lab.
Our general interest
Computational Materials and Process Design Technology on Hard Materials
(Metallic, Ionic, Semiconducting and Nano Device Materials),
through  an Understanding of Fundamental Materials Properties
(Thermodynamic, Kinetic and Atomic/Nano Structural Evolution),
based on  Atomistic Simulations, First-Principles Calculations and Computational Thermodynamics

2023년 1월 현재, 전산재료과학 연구실은 지도교수의 정년이 5년 미만 남음에 따라 더 이상 석박사 통합과정 학생을 받지는 못하며, 석사과정 또는 전산재료과학분야에서 석사를 마친 박사과정 학생만을 받을 수 있음을 알립니다.
—————————————————————
전산재료과학 연구실은 직접적인 소재 개발보다는 훗날 있게 될 다양한 첨단 소재의 연구개발 수행 기초 능력 배양이 가장 중요하다는 교육 철학을 가지고 운영되고 있습니다. 당 연구실은 computational thermodynamics 및 atomistic simulation을 주력 연구 수단으로 하며, 그 출발점이 되는 thermodynamic/interatomic potential database 개발 분야에서 국제적인 경쟁력을 갖추고 있습니다. 이를 기반으로 atomistic approach를 통해 나노 구조물 또는 나노 소재의 구조 및 기계 특성, first principles calculation과의 결합을 통해 나소 소재/소자의 기능 특성, kinetic Monte Carlo simulation과의 결합을 통해 구조 재료의 미세조직 특성 등을 분석/예측하고 design하는 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 학위과정 중에는 다양한 실험 연구 그룹과의 공동 연구를 통해 학제간 공동 연구 수행 경험, 이론 연구 결과의 실제 활용 경험을 쌓게 됩니다.
위와 같은 연구 수행을 위해 전산재료과학 연구실에서 첫 학기를 시작하는 석사 신입생들이 공부하게 되는 내용을 요약합니다. 석사 첫 학기에는 Computational Thermodynamics, Atomistic Simulation의 ABC를 이해한 후 ThermoCalc, KissMD&MC 등 관련 프로그램 사용 방법을 완벽히 숙지하는 것을 목표로 합니다.  첫 학기 후 방학 기간에는 기초 과제 수행을 통해 보고서/논문 작성법과 presentation 기법 등을 훈련하며, 2학기부터는 본격적인 개인 연구 과제와 기초를 다지기 위한 공부(강의 수강)를 시작합니다.  전산재료과학 연구실에서 Computational Thermodynamics와 Atomistic Simulation 기법은 필수이며, 개인 성향에 따라 First Principles Calculation 또는 Kinetic MonteCarlo Simulation을 병합하여 개인 차원의 전산재료과학 연구체계를 완성하게 됩니다.
1. 개강 전 (입학 전 방학 2개월)
1.1. Introduction to computational thermodynamics and application
- "
전산재료과학
”
홍릉과학출판사
part 1
- "Computational thermodynamics” Cambridge
- Thermodynamic Assessment
를
통해
ThermoCalc
사용법
Master
2. 학기 중
2.1. Fundamentals of Atomistic Simulation
- "
전산재료과학
”
홍릉과학출판사
part 2
- "Molecular Dynamics Simulation: Elementary
Methods" John Wiley & Sons, Inc.
2.2. Atomistic Simulation
- 기본 기법 및 code 이해
- KISSMD, KISSMC 사용법 Master
- Atomic Potential (2NN MEAM, 2NN MEAM+Qeq) 이해
3. 첫 학기 후 방학 중
3.1  기초 과제 수행, 보고서 작성
3.2  보고서, 논문 작성 방법, Presentation 기법 훈련
3.3  첫 학기 연구 경험을 통해 분야를 선택하고, 해당 분야에서
스스로 부족한 학술 분야의 강의 수강 계획 작성
4. 두번째 학기부터
4.1  연구원으로서의 기초 능력 확장 (강의 수강)
4.2  개인 연구 과제 수행 (주 1회 지도교수 면담)
4.3  연 4회 term paper 작성, Lab 세미나 발표
5. 국제학회 참석
5.1  석사 과정: 1회 포스터 발표, 박사 과정: 년 1회 구두 발표
5.2  학회 참석 전 초록집 분석 후 학회 활동 계획서 발표, 참석 후 간략 보고서 작성

Numerical Methods for Materials Scientist
재료공학을 이론적으로 연구하는 과정에서 유도된 제반 수학문제의 해를 컴퓨터를 이용하여 수치적인 방법으로 계산할 수 있는 능력을 배양함을 목표로 한다.
기초이론을 통해 수치해석에서 기본적으로 사용되는 이론을 습득하고 실습을 통해 실제적인 문제에 적용하는 방법을 배운다.
To enhance the capability for obtaining solutions of governing equations related to the materials science and engineering
by numerical methods, the students will learn basic numerical theories and how to define their problems and solve them via computer simulations.

전산재료과학 입문 (Introduction to Computational Materials Science)

Introduction of 2NN MEAM
The modified embedded atom method (MEAM) potential is the first semi-empirical interatomic
potential formalism that showed the possibility that one single formalism can be applied to a wide
range of elements including fcc, bcc, hcp, diamond-structured elements, and even gaseous
elements.
M.I. Baskes, Phys. Rev. B 46, 2727 (1992)
M.I. Baskes and R.A. Johnson, Modell. Simul. Mater. Sci. Eng. 2, 147 (1994)
The origianl MEAM formalism was modified to solve some stability problems, extending the interaction range to the second nearest-neighbor partially. The modified formalism is named the second nearest-neighbor (2NN) MEAM.
B.-J. Lee and M.I. Baskes, Phys. Rev. B 62, 8564 (2000)
B.-J. Lee, M.I. Baskes, H. Kim, and Y.K. Cho, Phys. Rev. B 64, 184102 (2001)
2NN MEAM in KISSMD / LAMMPS
KISSMD :
KISSMD (Kinetic Simulation System based on molecular dynamics) is an in-house MD simulation code
that uses the 2NN MEAM interatomic potential formalism.
LAMMPS :
The present 2NN MEAM formalism was recently (Feb. 14, 2011) implemented on the LAMMPS-MEAM engine in a collaboration with Dr. Greg Wagner, Sandia National Lab.

http://cmse.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 이병주 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 신소재공학과 교수로 전산재료과학(Computational Materials Science and Engineering) 분야를 담당하며 CMSE 연구실을 이끌고 있습니다. 서울대학교 금속공학과에서 1984년 학사, 1989년 박사학위를 받았고, 한국표준과학연구원(KRISS)과 스웨덴 KTH에서 박사후연구원 및 책임연구원으로 근무한 경력이 있습니다. 연구는 원자단위 전산모사, 제일원리계산, CALPHAD 기반 전산열역학을 축으로 금속·이온·반도체·나노소자 소재의 열역학적·속도론적 특성과 미세조직 변화를 예측하고 소재·공정을 설계하는 데 초점을 두고 있습니다. 대표 성과로 M.I. Baskes와 함께 제2최인접 수정 매립원자법(2NN MEAM) 원자간 포텐셜 형식을 제안했으며(Phys. Rev. B, 2000), KISSMD·KISSMC 전산모사 코드와 강재용 열역학 데이터베이스 TCFE2000 등 포텐셜·열역학 데이터베이스를 구축해 왔습니다. 최근에는 응고 현상의 몬테카를로 포츠 모델(Nature Communications 게재 예정), 분자동역학 기반 확산계수 계산의 기계학습 가속, 금속 적층제조 키홀 깊이에 대한 열유동 해석 등의 공동 저자 논문을 발표했습니다.

Biopolymer-based devices
1. Biopolymer-based RRAM
A memory device based on natural organic material is a promising device toward the next generation of nonvolatile nano-electronics. A solution-processed memory device based on chitosan as a natural solid polymer electrolyte can be switched reproducibly between high and low resistance states. In addition, the data retention measurement confirmed the reliability of the chitosan-based nonvolatile memory device. The transparent Ag-embedded chitosan film showed an acceptable and comparable resistive switching behavior on the flexible plastic substrate as well. A cost-effective, environmentally benign memory device using chitosan satisfies the functional requirements of nonvolatile memory operations.
2. Biopolymer-based synapses
The development of electronic devices possessing the functionality of biological synapses is a crucial step toward replicating the capabilities of the human brain. Of the various materials that have been used to realize artificial synapses, renewable natural materials have the advantages of being abundant, inexpensive, biodegradable, and ecologically benign. We report biocompatible artificial synapses based on biopolymers. These artificial synapses can emulate several essential synaptic behaviors including analog memory switching, the short-term plasticity, long-term plasticity, spike-rate-dependent plasticity, and short-term to long-term transition. These results suggest that a biopolymer can be a promising key component for artificial synapses.

Introduction
Resistive switching memory (RRAM)
RRAM is a type of device that exhibit resistive switching between a high-resistance state (HRS) and a low-resistance state (LRS). Its structure is simply an active material sandwiched between two metal electrodes, which is called metal-insulator-metal (MIM) structure. The advantages of RRAM are high read/write speed, low power consumption, high reliability, and scalability with simple structure. The expectation for RRAM is that: (1) it will be a new memory technology that can be integrated with conventional CMOS technology, and (2) it can be stacked in a 3D crosspoint architechture with a memory cell area of 4F
2
. Although there are numerous materials and approaches being reported, but property optimization based on deep understanding about resistive switching mechanism is required.
Neuromoprhic devices
We studied the behavior of artificial synapses. By controlling the filament formation and rupture, neuromorphic properties such as analog memory switching, short-term plasticity (STP), long-term plasticity (LTP), spike-rate-dependent plasticity, and short-term to long-term transition were demonstrated. Also, we demonstrated flexible neuromorphic devices by utilizing biomaterials. Biomaterial-based flexible artificial synapse devices emulated STP, paired-pulse facilitation, and transition from STP to LTP of a biological synapse without noticeable degradation under mechanical bending test. The above-mentioned neuromorphic characteristics were realized by exploiting the similarities between the silver or oxygen ion dynamics in the active materials and the Ca
2+
dynamics in a biological synapse. The development of electronic devices possessing the functionality of biological synapses is a crucial step toward mimicking the capabilities of the human brain.
Selector devices
Cross-point array is a good candidate for future high density memory device due to 3D configuration with small cell size of 4F
2
. However, the cross-point array has critical problems with interconnected series resistance and undesired current leakage path, which can lead to misreading of information stored in the selected cell. Selector device has been introduced to alleviate these problems.

Perovskite-based devices
1.  Resistive switching memory
Hysteresis in
organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites (
OIPs) is a result of defect migration under an electric ﬁeld. This phenomenon has potential applications in computer memory. Especially, the hysteretic behavior which is explained by the ion migration under electric ﬁeld can extend the OIP material applications to resistive switching memories and artiﬁcial synapses. Our lab focused on resistive switching effect by halide-ion migration (e.g., migration of iodine vacancies) which have potential to be applied in next generation memory.
2. Photodetector
Our research is the applications of organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites (OIPs) to optoelectronic device such as photodetector. Moreover, integrating two-dimensional (2D) OIPs with the 2D materials including graphenes give opportunities for various options in constructing new types of heterojunctions with novel functionalities including enhanced charge transport properties. Ferroelectric devices
1. CMOS-compatible ferreoelctric NAND flash memory
The next-generation ferroelectric memory has gained attention so far for its potential to operate at higher speed with lower power consumption compared to the conventional flash memory. But its commercialization has been deterred due to the high processing temperature, difficulty in scaling, and non-compatibility with the conventional semiconductor processes. Our lab presented unique integration strategies to overcome these issues by introducing the hafnia-based ferroelectrics and oxide semiconductors. The new material and structure ensured low power consumption and high speed, and achieved high stability by using oxide semiconductors as channel material to lower the process temperature and suppress the formation of the unwanted interface layer. As a result, the fabricated device could operate at a voltage four times lower than that of the conventional flash memory at a speed several hundred times faster and remain stable even when repeatedly used more than 100 million times. In particular, a ferroelectric material and an oxide semiconductor were stacked by an atomic layer deposition to secure a processing technology suitable for manufacturing 3D devices. This study suggested that ALD-based
ferroelectric thin film transistor
s have the potential in future high-density 3D memory applications.
2. Ferroelectric analog synaptic transistor
Neuromorphic computing is a promising alternative to conventional computing systems as it could enable parallel computation and adaptive learning process. However, the development of energy efficient neuromorphic hardware systems has been hindered by the limited performance of analog synaptic devices. Here, we demonstrate the analog conductance modulation behavior in the ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFT) that have the nanoscale ferroelectric material and oxide semiconductors. Accurate control of polarization changes in the nanoscale ferroelectric layer induces conductance modulation to demonstrate linear potentiation and depression characteristics of FeTFTs. Our devices show potentiation and depression properties, including high linearity, multiple states, and small cycle-to-cycle/device-to-device variations. In simulations with measured properties, a neuromorphic system with FeTFT achieves 91.1% recognition accuracy of handwritten digits. This work may provide a way to realize the neuromorphic hardware systems that use FeTFTs as the synaptic devices.
3. Photonic synapses based on ferroelectric material and oxide semiconductor
A number of synapse devices have been intensively studied for the neuromorphic system which is the next‐generation energy‐efficient computing method. Among these various types of synapse devices, photonic synapse devices recently attracted significant attention. In particular, the photonic synapse devices using persistent photoconductivity (PPC) phenomena in oxide semiconductors are receiving much attention due to the similarity between relaxation characteristics of PPC phenomena and Ca
2+
dynamics of biological synapses. However, these devices have limitations in its controllability of the relaxation characteristics of PPC behaviors. To utilize the oxide semiconductor as photonic synapse devices, relaxation behavior needs to be accurately controlled. In this study, a photonic synapse device with controlled relaxation characteristics by using an oxide semiconductor and a ferroelectric layer is demonstrated. This device exploits the PPC characteristics to demonstrate synaptic functions including short‐term plasticity, paired‐pulse facilitation (PPF), and long‐term plasticity (LTP). The relaxation properties are controlled by the polarization of the ferroelectric layer, and this polarization is used to control the amount by which the conductance levels increase during PPF operation and to enhance LTP characteristics. This study provides an important step toward the development of photonic synapses with tunable synaptic functions.

Low-power selector devices
Cross-point memory device structure has recently been attracted considerable attention as the future device technology. However, the undesired sneak currents originated from low-resistance state of ReRAM cells may induce sensing errors and high power consumption. To solve this problem, it is necessary to use switch devices that can turn active devices on and off effectively. For this purpose, high on/off current selectivity with ultra-low off-current and high on-current is required. Here, we report a novel switch behavior with over 109 selectivity, a high on-current density of 1 MA cm-2, an ultra-low off-current density of 1 mA cm-2, excellent thermal stability up to 250 °C and abrupt turn-on with 5 mV per decade in solution-processed silver-doped zinc oxide thin films. The selection behavior is attributed to light doping of silver ions in zinc oxide films during electrochemical deposition to generate atomic-scale narrow conduction paths, which can be formed and ruptured at low voltages.

Bottom-up process
1. Self-assembly
We investigated the effect of increasing the number of polyelectrolyte and gold nanoparticle layers on memory performance, including the size of the memory window (the critical voltage difference between the ‘programmed’ and ‘erased’ states of the devices) and programming speed. We observed a maximum memory window of about 1.8 V, with a stored electron density of 4.2 x 10
12
cm
-2
in the gold nanoparticle layers, when the devices consist of three polyelectrolyte/gold nanoparticle layers. The reported approach offers new opportunities to prepare nanostructured polyelectrolyte/gold nanoparticle-based memory devices with tailored performance.
2. Anodized aluminum oxide (AAO)
Nanoscale resistive switching memory cells with controlled cell sizes in the range of 25 to 90 nm were successfully fabricated using anodized aluminum oxide templates, and their electrical properties were directly measured using a conductive atomic force microscope. The size of the memory cells was systematically controlled by controlling the pore size of the nanoscale masks. The devices exhibited controllable and reliable resistive switching characteristics suitable for programmable memory applications. The reported approach provides new opportunities for the preparation of nanostructured nonvolatile memory devices with continued device scaling.
3. Electrochemical deposition (ECD)
We report a feasible and versatile way to fabricate high-density, nanoscale memory devices by direct bottom-up filling of memory elements. An ordered array of metal/oxide/metal (copper/copper oxide/copper) nanodots was synthesized with a uniform size and thickness defined by self-organized nanotemplate mask by sequential electrochemical deposition (ECD) of each layer. The fabricated memory devices showed bipolar resistive switching behaviors confirmed by conductive atomic force microscopy. This study demonstrates that ECD with bottom-up growth has great potential to fabricate high-density nanoelectronic devices beyond the scaling limit of top-down device fabrication processes.
