“같은 사용자라도 출근 중과 주말에는 무엇을 다르게 추천해야 할까요?”
연구에서 연결하려는 정보
사용자 ↔ 선호 ↔ 현재 상황 ↔ 사용 가능한 서비스 ↔ 추천 후보. 개인화된 디지털 트윈과 지식 증강을 활용하여 추천에 필요한 맥락을 표현합니다.
01 / KNOWLEDGE SCHEMA
온톨로지 구축
도메인의 개념과 관계를 정의하고, 문서와 데이터에서 얻은 지식을 일관된 구조에 연결합니다.
02 / CONTEXTUAL LEARNING
관계를 활용한 표현과 추론
그래프 기반 표현학습과 LLM을 연결하여 추천·검색·추론에 필요한 맥락을 활용합니다.
03 / EVIDENCE & GOVERNANCE
출처·변경·권한의 고려
정보의 근거, 최신성, 접근 권한을 함께 다루는 방향을 탐구합니다. 그래프 사용만으로 정답이나 보안이 보장되지는 않습니다.

Queueing-Informed Machine Learning
Queueing-Informed Machine Learning
대기이론을,
학습의 구조로 사용합니다.
도착, 처리, 혼잡과 용량의 관계를 데이터와 함께 학습합니다. 대기모형에서 유도한 미분방정식을 학습 목적함수에 반영하는 것이 핵심입니다.
운영시스템에도, 따라야 할 동역학이 있습니다.
관측값을 잘 맞추는 것만으로 시스템의 시간적 거동을 충분히 설명할 수 있을까요? QIML은 대기이론의 유체근사 등에서 얻은 구조를 머신러닝에 연결하여, 데이터 적합도와 시스템 동역학의 일관성을 함께 고려합니다.
QUEUEING THEORY AS OPERATIONAL PHYSICS
제조 공정, 서비스 시스템 등에서 일감과 고객의 유입·처리·축적을 설명하는 원리를 학습의 지식으로 활용합니다.
QIML · 관측 + 대기 동역학
모바일에서는 좌우로 이동
관측과 대기모형을 신경망 학습에 연결하는 QIML: 상태 추정에서 데이터 오차와 대기모형 잔차를 계산하고 결합 손실로 학습한다
대기이론에서 유도한 동역학
dq/dt = λ(t) − μ min(q(t), n)

시간 · 관측된 시스템 상태

관측 적합도 + 동역학 일관성
자동미분
파라미터 업데이트 · 데이터와 이론의 균형
연구실 세미나의 Queueing-Informed Neural Network 구조를 단순화했습니다. 위 미분방정식은 단순한 Mₜ/M/n 유체근사 예시이며, 모든 대기시스템의 정확한 방정식이 아닙니다.
01 / DYNAMICS
대기모형의 동적 구조
대기시스템의 유체·확산 근사 등에서 얻는 구조를 학습에 어떻게 반영할지 연구합니다.
02 / LIMITED OBSERVATIONS
불완전한 관측의 활용
관측이 부족하거나 결측이 존재하는 구간에서 데이터와 모형 지식을 함께 활용하는 상태 추정·보완을 연구합니다.
03 / MODEL MISMATCH
근사모형과 현실의 차이
동역학 제약의 강도, 모형의 가정, 실제 시스템과의 차이가 학습 결과에 미치는 영향을 검토합니다.

http://www.lstlab.org/.summary: 고영명(Young Myoung Ko) 교수는 POSTECH 산업경영공학과 확률시스템 연구실(LST Lab.)을 이끌며, 확률과정·대기이론·최적화의 수학적 기반 위에서 불확실성 모델링을 실제 시스템의 의사결정으로 연결하는 산업 AI 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 주요 연구축은 제조·소재 파운데이션 모델(MFM·MatFM), 개인화 추천과 기업 문서 맥락 이해를 위한 Graph Ontology, 그리고 대기모형에서 유도한 동역학을 학습 목적함수에 반영하는 Queueing-Informed Machine Learning 세 가지입니다. 최근에는 시계열 파운데이션 모델 기반 이상 탐지 연구(NeurIPS 2026 GAPS, ICLR 2026, TMLR 2026 등)와 효율적 데이터 수집을 위한 단조 변분 가우시안 프로세스(ICML 2026) 연구에 교신저자로 참여했습니다. 연구과제로는 산업통상부의 제조 특화 파운데이션 모델(MFM) 핵심 기술 개발, AI 기반 소재 물성예측 파운데이션 모델 개발, 삼성전자의 멀티모달 그래프 기반 사용자 표현 학습 과제 등을 수행하고 있습니다. 또한 2025년 산업통상부 장관표창과 IISE Transactions Service Award를 받았고, 2026년 ICIEA에서 제조·서비스 시스템을 위한 파운데이션 모델을 주제로 기조강연을 맡았습니다.

인사말
Welcome to the Quality Systems Laboratory, Department of Industrial and Management Engineering, Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH). Today, many firms are faced with rapid changes stimulated by innovations and dynamic customer demands. Providing high-quality products/services to customer in a timely manner is crucial for the companies’survival in the competitive marketplace. Research at the Quality Systems Laboratory is focused on the modeling and analysis of new products and process design activities, with an emphasis on quality improvement. Our research program has produced significant results on several fronts, and has been very well received by the government and industry as well as academia. We feel especially proud of the laboratory’s graduates who are now playing important roles at various leading organizations. We will continue to do our best to accomplish the laboratory’s vision, namely to "Develop world-class graduates and research results in the field of quality systems innovation."
포항공과대학교 산업경영공학과의 품질시스템 연구실 홈페이지 방문을 환영합니다. 오늘날 많은 기업들이 기술혁신과 소비자 요구의 다양화로 인한 급격한 변화를 경험하고 있습니다. 이들의 생존여부는 소비자가 원하는 품질의 제품 및 서비스를 효과적으로 개발하는 능력을 갖추고 있는가에 달려 있습니다. 결국 품질은 기업생존의 핵심입니다. 품질시스템 연구실은 신제품/서비스의 개발에 관련된 제반 품질문제의 모델링 및 분석에 대한 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 저희의 연구 결과가 국내외 학계 및 산업계로부터 많은 각광을 받고 있고, 또한 저희 연구실의 졸업생들이 국내외의 유수한 기관에서 훌륭히 활약하고 있음을 매우 자랑스럽게 생각합니다. 품질시스템 연구실은 품질시스템 분야에서 세계 최고 수준의 졸업생 배출과 연구업적을 이룩한다는 연구실의 비전을 달성하기 위하여 최선의 노력을 경주하겠습니다. 감사합니다.

연구실 비전
품질시스템 연구실의 목표
품질 시스템 분야를 선도하는 졸업생을 배출하고 세계 최고 수준의 연구 성과를 이룩한다.
1. 품질시스템 분야를
제품/서비스 품질 향상에 관한 최신 기술에 대한 연구를 수행한다.
학계와 산업계의 지속 가능한 혁신을 지향하는 연구를 수행한다.
2. 선도하는 졸업생을 배출하고
탁월성, 창의성, 성실성을 고무시킬 수 있는 연구 환경을 제공한다.
독립적인 연구자로 성장할 수 있도록 지도한다.
자유로운 연구 분위기 속에서 함께 성장할 수 있는 시너지를 창출한다.
3. 세계 최고 수준의 연구 성과를 이룩한다.
활발한 학술 교류를 통해 연구 실적을 학계에 공유한다.

연구분야
고객 가치는 기업 경쟁력의 핵심입니다. 뛰어난 고객 가치의 창출과 제공은 끊임없는 품질 혁신의 기반 위에서만 가능합니다. 품질시스템 연구실에서는 제품 및 서비스의 품질 혁신을 위한 이론 및 응용 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 특히, 최근의 시대 흐름에 발맞추어 본 연구실은 시스템적 관점에서 ‘제품’과 ‘서비스’의 품질 혁신을 연구하고 있으며, 연구 분야는 품질공학과 서비스공학으로 구성됩니다.
품질공학
품질공학은 고객 가치의 제공을 위해 제품, 서비스의 품질을 향상시키는 데에 필요한 제반 방법을 연구하는 학문입니다. 품질공학의 핵심 영역은 제품 설계, 공정 설계, 그리고 제품 생산으로 나뉘는데, 제품 설계 단계에서는 QFD 등을 활용하여 고객의 요구사항이 충실히 반영된 제품을 설계하게 됩니다. 공정 설계 단계에서는 실험계획법, Taguchi 방법 등을 활용하여 제품을 생산하는 공정을 설계하고 최적화합니다. 생산 단계에서는 SPC 등을 활용하여 제품 생산과정을 모니터링하고 관리합니다. 품질시스템 연구실은 고객지향, 실용적인 방법론의 개발을 위해 노력하고 있습니다.
위 그림은 품질공학의 연구 프레임워크입니다. 이는 크게 Product Design, Process Design, 그리고 Production 분야로 구성되어 있습니다. 이들 연구의 공동적인 목적은 고객 만족 증대, 품질 비용 감소를 통한 품질 경영의 달성입니다. 세 가지 분야와 관련하여 본 연구실에서 수행 중인 연구는 그림의 각 항목 아래에 간략히 서술되어 있습니다.
서비스공학
서비스공학은 서비스 산업의 경쟁력 강화와 서비스 혁신을 위한 과학적인 방법을 연구하는 학문입니다. 서비스공학의 핵심 영역은 서비스 개발, 운영, 개선 등으로 나뉩니다. 서비스 개발 단계에서는 서비스 컨셉 설계, 서비스 프로세스 설계, 제조와 서비스의 통합화 등의 체계적 지원 방법론을 연구합니다. 서비스 운영 단계에서는 운영 중인 서비스의 품질을 관리, 평가 및 분석할 수 있는 체계를 연구합니다. 서비스 개선 단계에서는 현재의 품질을 개선하고, 새로운 차원의 서비스를 제공하려는 연구를 진행합니다. 최근 IT 기술의 발전과 서비스공학의 결합은 서비스의 개발, 운영, 개선 측면에서 무궁무진한 기회를 만들고 있습니다.
위 그림은 서비스 혁신의 연구 프레임워크입니다. 이는 크게 Service Development, Service Operation, 그리고 Service Improvement 분야로 구성되어 있습니다. 이들 연구의 공동적인 목적은 고객 만족 증대, 고객 충성도 제고를 통한 고객 가치 경영입니다. 세가지 분야와 관련하여 본 연구실에서 수행 중인 연구는 그림의 각 항목 아래에 간략히 서술되어 있습니다.

http://quality.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 김광재 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 산업경영공학과 교수로 품질시스템 연구실을 이끌고 있으며, 서울대학교 산업공학 학사와 한국과학기술원 산업공학 석사를 거쳐 Purdue University에서 경영과학 박사학위를 받았다. 1994년부터 1997년까지 Pennsylvania State University 산업공학과 조교수를 지낸 뒤 1997년 POSTECH에 부임해 조교수와 부교수를 거쳐 2005년부터 교수로 재직했고, 연세대학교 겸임교수와 중국 동북재경대학교 객좌교수 등도 역임했다. 주요 관심 분야는 품질공학과 서비스공학으로, 제품 설계(QFD), 공정 설계(실험계획법·다구치 방법), 생산 단계의 통계적 공정관리(SPC)를 아우르는 품질 혁신 방법론과 서비스 개발·운영·개선 방법론을 연구한다. 한국연구재단 지원의 'Industrial Internet Platform 기반의 혁신적인 제품 품질 관리 방법 개발', '클라우드 제조 시스템의 제품 품질 향상을 위한 리소스 진단 체계 개발', '빅데이터 분석 기반의 적응형 공정 관리 체계 개발' 등 다수 과제를 연구책임자로 수행했으며, 산업통상자원부의 스마트 안전 리빙랩 구축 사업에도 참여기관 연구책임자로 참여했다. 최근에는 반도체 웨이퍼 테스트 데이터의 결측치 대체, 잠재 결함 칩 검출, 다단계·다중설비 공정의 결함 의심 설비 선별, 스마트홈·스마트안전 서비스의 사용자경험 평가 등을 주제로 국내외 저널 논문과 학회 발표를 이어왔다.

POSTECH · Factory Intelligence Laboratory
AI-Native Manufacturing Systems
We develop manufacturing systems that are readable, reasonable, actionable, and learnable for AI.
Our research integrates control semantics, autonomous agents, digital twins, physics-aware simulation, domain-robust fault diagnosis, and causal quality analytics to build the next generation of intelligent and adaptive factories.

Research Theme
AI-ready factories of the future
Vision
Toward manufacturing systems that AI can understand, reason about, act upon, and learn from.
Conventional manufacturing systems are primarily designed for human engineers: drawings, control logic, process rules, and operating procedures are often fragmented, implicit, and difficult for AI to interpret.
FILab transforms factories into AI-native environments by developing semantic representations, simulation models, optimization methods, digital twins, and learning algorithms that make manufacturing knowledge executable for AI agents.
AI-Native Properties
What makes manufacturing AI-native?
We make production systems structured enough for AI to read, model, execute, and improve them across machines, workcells, and factories.
R
AI-Readable
Manufacturing knowledge, control logic, process flows, and equipment states are represented in structured forms that AI systems can interpret.
R
AI-Reasonable
AI can infer operational constraints, causal relationships, control semantics, and process dependencies from manufacturing representations.
A
AI-Actionable
AI decisions can be translated into executable actions through digital twins, control programs, robotic systems, and automation interfaces.
L
AI-Learnable
Manufacturing systems continuously improve by learning from production data, fault patterns, quality outcomes, and human tacit knowledge.
Research Pillars
Two pillars for AI-native manufacturing
01
AI-Native Machine Control and Operations Autonomy
Control semantics architecture, autonomous workcell agents, digital twins as AI decision spaces, physics-aware virtual commissioning, and human tacit knowledge for robotic learning.
Factory Control
02
Next-Generation Fault Detection, Prognostics, and Causal Quality Analytics
Continual and source-free domain adaptation, open-set and target-free domain generalization, diffusion-assisted cross-domain fault diagnosis, and process-genealogy mining.
Factory Analytics
Software in Action
AI-native tools for virtual programming and autonomous workcell operation.
Our software platforms demonstrate how manufacturing semantics, digital twins, and agent-based interfaces can turn workcell knowledge into executable control and operation workflows.

Factory Control | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
Factory Control
Factory Control studies AI-native machine control and operations autonomy: how AI can understand control semantics, act through workcell agents, reason inside digital twins, and validate robotic assembly logic before deployment.
Research Stack
Control Semantics Â· Agents Â· Digital Twins
Research Directions
AI-Native Machine Control and Operations Autonomy
01
Control Semantics Architecture
Semantic representation for AI-native machine control, including Control Semantic Graphs, Part Travel Plans, device grounding, and the semantic-to-control process for generating and validating industrial logic.
More
02
AI Agent for Autonomous Workcell
AI agents that perceive workcell states, coordinate devices, make operation decisions, and adapt execution under changing production conditions.
More
03
Digital Twin as an AI Decision Space
Executable digital twin environments where AI agents can simulate candidate actions, evaluate control consequences, and refine operation strategies before deployment.
More
04
Physics-Aware AI for Virtual Commissioning
Validation of robotic assembly control logic by combining physical constraints, simulation models, and AI-based reasoning in virtual commissioning.
More
05
Human Tacit Knowledge for Robotic Learning
Integration of expert know-how, demonstrations, and implicit operation rules into robotic learning and autonomous execution.
More

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.title: Control Semantics Architecture | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.text:
Control Semantics Architecture | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
Control Semantics Architecture
A semantic architecture that makes manufacturing control readable, reasonable, actionable, and learnable for AI.
Control Semantic Graph
Part Travel Plan
Device Grounding
ConditionâAction Logic
Semantic Verification
From physical workcells to control semantics
We represent devices, I/O signals, task flows, state transitions, safety rules, and operation constraints as structured control semantics rather than isolated ladder fragments or human-only documents.
CSG, PTP, and grounded control meaning
Control Semantic Graphs and Part Travel Plans provide AI-interpretable views of workpart flow, device roles, condition-action relations, and execution dependencies. These representations ground high-level manufacturing intent to concrete sensors, actuators, and PLC tags.
Semantic-to-control process
The long-term goal is to transform multimodal manufacturing information into semantic views, build control semantic graphs, derive intermediate control representations, and generate or verify executable industrial control programs.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.title: AI Agent for Autonomous Workcell | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.text:
AI Agent for Autonomous Workcell | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
AI Agent for Autonomous Workcell
AI agents that operate manufacturing workcells by perceiving states, making decisions, coordinating devices, and adapting execution.
Perception
Decision-Making
Device Coordination
Adaptive Execution
Autonomous workcell operation
A workcell agent observes machine states, interprets workpart progress, selects next actions, and coordinates devices such as robots, sensors, fixtures, and controllers.
Agentic decision loop
The agent links perception, reasoning, digital-twin simulation, and execution so that operation decisions can be evaluated before being issued to physical systems.
From control rules to operational autonomy
Instead of only executing pre-written logic, the workcell agent enables adaptive control and operation strategies under product variation, disturbance, and reconfiguration.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.title: Digital Twin as an AI Decision Space | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.text:
Digital Twin as an AI Decision Space | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
Digital Twin as an AI Decision Space
Executable digital twins where AI agents can simulate, compare, and improve manufacturing decisions before acting in real systems.
Executable Twin
What-if Simulation
Look-ahead Reasoning
Agent Decision Space
Beyond visualization
A digital twin is treated not only as a visual replica but as an executable decision space where AI can test candidate actions and observe their consequences.
Look-ahead reasoning
Agents can run what-if simulations, compare control strategies, estimate cycle time and safety impacts, and select actions that are robust to changing workcell states.
Closed-loop learning environment
The digital twin connects virtual commissioning, operation monitoring, and learning from execution traces to improve future control and scheduling decisions.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.title: Physics-Aware AI for Virtual Commissioning | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.text:
Physics-Aware AI for Virtual Commissioning | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
Physics-Aware AI for Virtual Commissioning
Physics-aware AI for validating robotic assembly control logic in virtual commissioning before deployment.
Robotic Assembly
Physical Constraints
Virtual Commissioning
Logic Validation
Control logic must satisfy physics
Robotic assembly control cannot be validated only by logical sequence. It must also respect reachability, collision, contact, tolerance, motion feasibility, and fixture constraints.
Physics-aware validation
We combine simulation models, physical constraints, and AI reasoning to detect invalid or risky control logic before it is deployed to real equipment.
Virtual commissioning for robotic assembly
The approach supports early debugging of robot paths, interlocks, assembly sequences, and safety rules inside a digital twin-based commissioning environment.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.title: Human Tacit Knowledge for Robotic Learning | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/factory.text:
Human Tacit Knowledge for Robotic Learning | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Control
Human Tacit Knowledge for Robotic Learning
Methods for integrating expert know-how, demonstrations, and implicit operation rules into robotic learning and autonomous execution.
Tacit Knowledge
Demonstration Learning
Robotic Learning
Human-in-the-loop AI
Tacit knowledge as learning signal
Experienced operators often know subtle handling rules, exception cases, and process tricks that are not written in formal manuals. We aim to capture such tacit knowledge as useful learning signals.
From demonstration to robotic policy
Human demonstrations, voice instructions, annotations, and operation traces can be translated into task constraints, preferred actions, and correction signals for robotic learning.
Human-in-the-loop autonomy
The goal is not to remove human expertise, but to make it reusable by AI agents and robots in autonomous workcell operation.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/oandm/A.title: Adaptive Fault Detection and Prognostics | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/oandm/A.text:
Adaptive Fault Detection and Prognostics | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Analytics
Adaptive Fault Detection and Prognostics
Self-learning and transferable AI for detecting faults, predicting failures, and adapting across machines, products, and operating conditions.
Continual Domain Adaptation
Source-Free Domain Adaptation
Open-Set Generalization
Target-Free Generalization
Diffusion-Assisted Diagnosis
Domain shifts in manufacturing
Fault diagnosis models often fail when machine type, operating condition, product specification, sensor setting, or factory environment changes. Adaptive learning addresses this domain-shift problem.
Five research directions
We investigate continual domain adaptation, source-free domain adaptation, open-set domain generalization, domain generalization without target adaptation, and diffusion-assisted cross-domain fault diagnosis.
Toward reliable prognostics
The goal is to build fault detection and prognostics models that remain reliable under unseen faults, limited labels, privacy constraints, and changing production domains.

http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/oandm/M.title: Multi-stage Quality Causality | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
http://fi.postech.ac.kr/projects/oandm/M.text:
Multi-stage Quality Causality | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Analytics
Multi-stage Quality Causality
Causal process-genealogy mining for explaining how process history and machine states affect downstream quality outcomes.
Causal Quality Analytics
Process Genealogy
Multi-stage Manufacturing
Root-Cause Explanation
Quality is generated across stages
Final quality is rarely caused by a single process step. It emerges from material history, machine states, process conditions, routing, rework, and upstream decisions across multiple stages.
Process-genealogy mining
We model the genealogy of parts, processes, machines, and inspections to discover how upstream variation propagates into downstream quality outcomes.
From prediction to explanation
The objective is not only to predict defects but also to identify causal factors, actionable process conditions, and intervention points for quality improvement.

Factory Analytics | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Analytics
Factory Analytics
Factory Analytics develops robust and transferable AI methods for diagnosing faults, predicting degradation, and discovering causal quality relationships across machines, products, processes, and domains.
Research Stack
Fault Detection Â· Prognostics Â· Causal Quality
Research Directions
Next-Generation Fault Detection, Prognostics, and Causal Quality Analytics
01
Feature Engineering & Process Fault Detection
Feature representation, signal analysis, and process fault detection methods for manufacturing monitoring and machine health assessment.
More
02
Adaptive Fault Detection and Prognostics
Continual domain adaptation, source-free adaptation, open-set domain generalization, target-free generalization, and diffusion-assisted cross-domain fault diagnosis.
More
03
Multi-stage Quality Causality
Causal process-genealogy mining for discovering how upstream process conditions, machine states, material histories, and decisions affect downstream quality.
More
04
Event-driven Machine Failure Analysis
Failure diagnosis using event logs and system-state transitions to reason about root causes, functional interactions, and product field failures.
More
05
Sound Source Localization
Noise detection and sound-source localization for acoustic quality monitoring in clamorous manufacturing environments.
More

Factory Design | Factory Intelligence Laboratory
Factory Design
Factory Design
Factory Design studies how human knowledge, rapid simulation modeling, and plant layout optimization can accelerate the design and improvement of manufacturing systems.
Research Stack
Human Knowledge Â· Simulation Â· Layout Optimization
Research Directions
Simulation-based design for future manufacturing systems
01
Voice of Workers
Human tacit knowledge, worker experience, and implicit operation know-how are captured and structured to support manufacturing design, robotic learning, and human-centered automation.
More
02
Rapid Simulation Modeling
Rapid creation of simulation models from neutral formats, layout analysis, feature extraction, and model generation for manufacturing system design.
More
03
Simulation-Based Plant Layout Optimization
Simulation-based plant layout optimization for evaluating alternatives, analyzing process flow, and improving productivity before physical deployment.
More

http://logistics.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 김병인 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 산업경영공학과 물류연구실(Logistics Lab)을 중심으로 물류·공급망관리 분야 연구를 수행하고 있습니다. 주요 연구 초점은 TSP, TSPTW, VRP, VRPTW, 주기적 VRPTW, 오리엔티어링 문제 등 차량경로 문제와 실제 산업용 최적화 응용(AMHS용 지능형 배차·경로 알고리즘 포함), 그리고 물류 시스템 시뮬레이션 모델링이며, 수리계획법·그래프 이론·메타휴리스틱·매쓰휴리스틱·동적계획법·강화학습 등의 방법론을 활용합니다. 연구 주제는 스쿨버스 경로, 폐기물 수거 VRPTW, 선박 경로, 2차원 빈 패킹, 수소 충전소 점진적 배치, 철강산업 기관차 경로 등 다양한 벤치마크 문제로 확장되어 있습니다. 특허로는 후판 날판의 설계 방법, 철강 연원료 배선계획 최적화, 운행 일정 생성, 철강 제품 배선 계획 수립, 무인운반차 주행 제어(한국 및 미국 US-11815909-B2 등록), 수소 충전소 점진적 배치 및 수소 공급망 설계 등이 있으며, 후판 날판 설계 방법은 2023년 POSCO로 기술이전되었고 택배 네트워크 최적화 및 도장공장 생산계획 알고리즘 등도 기업에 이전되었습니다. 교육 측면에서는 대학원 이산최적화(MEIE662)와 학부 정보시스템기술, 공급망관리, 생산관리, 시뮬레이션 과목을 담당하고 있습니다.

scalable priors

https://sites.google.com/view/sangwoomo.summary: 모상우 교수는 POSTECH 산업경영공학과 조교수(2025년 부임)로 인공지능대학원, Applied AI, 산업데이터사이언스 대학원에 겸임되어 있으며, KAIST에서 신진우 교수 지도로 박사학위를 받은 뒤 미시간대학교에서 Stella X. Yu 교수와 박사후연구원을 지냈습니다. 연구 목표는 AI를 위한 확장 가능한 사전지식(scalable priors) 설계로, 도메인 구조와 통계적 가정 같은 귀납적 편향을 접목해 비전·언어·로보틱스 전반의 성능과 신뢰성, 해석가능성을 높이는 데 초점을 두며, 본인이 이끄는 MOAI(Multimodal Orchestration of Artificial Intelligence) 연구실에서는 에이전틱 AI, 피지컬 AI, 제조 AI를 주요 주제로 삼고 있습니다. NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, CVPR, EMNLP, TMLR 등 주요 학회·저널에 공정한 확산모델(StayFair), 멀티모달 데이터셋 증류, 시각 편향 발견(B2T), 계층적 이미지 분할(CAST) 등 다수의 논문을 발표했고, ICCV 2025 SP4V 워크숍 조직위원과 ICLR 2027 Area Chair를 맡았습니다. 연구비 측면에서는 NRF의 AI for Operational Research, IITP의 멀티모달 장문맥 에이전트, KEIT의 제조 파운데이션 모델 및 전문가 수준 피지컬 AI 과제와 삼성전자의 AI 기반 반도체 설계 과제 등을 수행 중입니다. 또한 Google, Meta, NVIDIA 등 주요 연구소와 협업했고 삼성·퀄컴 펠로십을 받았으며, POSTECH에서 데이터 엔지니어링과 데이터사이언스 프로그래밍 과목을 강의하고 있습니다.

POSTECH · Industrial & Management Engineering
Turning data into intelligence for processes and decisions.
The Analytics & Information Management (AIM) Lab at POSTECH develops data-driven methods to
understand how processes work, determine what should happen next, and build intelligent solutions for real-world
problems.

Explore our research
Join the lab
Research areas
Six areas the lab works in. They overlap far more than they compete — most projects pull on several
at once.
Research area
Process Mining
Discovering, monitoring, and improving real-world processes from event data, including process discovery, conformance checking, object-centric process mining, event abstraction, and predictive process monitoring.
Research area
Recommender Systems
Developing personalized and context-aware recommendation methods, with a particular focus on fashion, customer preferences, and data-driven decision support.
Research area
Applied AI
Developing AI and machine learning methods for real-world problems, including deep learning, generative AI, large language models, and domain-specific foundation models.
Research area
AI-Driven Process Innovation
Combining process intelligence and AI to identify improvement opportunities, redesign workflows, automate decision-making, and develop new ways of working with human and AI collaboration.
Research area
Simulation & Digital Twins
Building data-driven simulation models and digital twins to understand, evaluate, and improve complex systems, particularly in manufacturing and healthcare.
Research area
Predictive & Prescriptive Analytics
Developing predictive and optimization methods to anticipate outcomes, recommend actions, allocate resources, and support better operational decisions.
Research in detail
About the Lab
The Analytics & Information Management (AIM) Lab at POSTECH conducts research at the intersection of
Process Mining, Recommender Systems, and Applied AI
. We develop data-driven methods to
understand how complex processes work, determine what should happen next, and build intelligent solutions for
real-world problems.
Our research combines
artificial intelligence, machine learning, simulation, optimization, and
digital twins
to discover, predict, and improve process behavior, provide personalized recommendations,
and support better operational decisions. Through these approaches, we aim to turn complex data into
actionable intelligence and measurable improvement
.
A defining feature of the AIM Lab is our
close collaboration with industry
. Our research has
been supported by the Korean government and leading companies including
Samsung Electronics, Samsung
C&T, HD Hyundai, and POSCO
, with projects spanning
manufacturing, healthcare, and the
fashion industry
. These long-term collaborations provide opportunities to develop and validate new
methods with real-world data and translate research into practical impact.
The lab has published
more than 150 scientific papers
in leading journals and conferences,
including
Decision Support Systems
,
Information Systems
,
Journal of Information
Technology
,
International Journal of Medical Informatics
, Business Process Management (BPM), and
the International Conference on Process Mining (ICPM).
We are equally committed to translating research into practice.
Puzzle Data
, Korea’s first
process mining software company, was established as a spin-off from the AIM Lab, bringing process mining
research into enterprise applications.
ZenAii Co.
, an AI-powered fashion recommendation
company, was also spun off from the lab, translating our research in recommender systems and AI into
personalized fashion services. Together, these ventures demonstrate our commitment to turning academic research
into technologies, solutions, and businesses with real-world impact.

Research — AIM Lab, POSTECH
Skip to content
What We Work On
Our research is centered on
Process Mining, Recommender Systems, and Applied AI
,
complemented by
AI-Driven Process Innovation, Simulation & Digital Twins, and Predictive &
Prescriptive Analytics
.
Together, these areas enable us to understand complex processes, predict what happens next,
recommend better actions, and develop intelligent solutions for real-world problems.
Process Mining
We develop methods to
discover, analyze, predict, and improve real-world processes from event data
, transforming operational data into actionable process intelligence.
Object-centric process mining
and process discovery
Event abstraction
, conformance checking, and predictive monitoring
Process visualization, organizational mining, and process optimization
Recommender Systems
We develop
personalized and context-aware recommendation technologies
that help users make better choices, with a particular focus on the
fashion industry
.
Personalized
product, outfit, and fashion recommendation
User preference and behavioral modeling
Context-aware and AI-enhanced recommendation
Applied AI
We develop and apply
AI and machine learning technologies to real-world problems
, combining advanced models with domain knowledge and operational data.
Generative AI, large language models, and AI agents
Domain-specific foundation models
Deep learning, multimodal AI, and explainable AI
AI-Driven Process Innovation
We combine
process intelligence and AI to redesign how organizations operate
, moving beyond process analysis toward intelligent and adaptive ways of working.
AI-assisted
process redesign and improvement
Generative AI and agents for process innovation
Human–AI collaboration
and intelligent workflow automation
Simulation & Digital Twins
We build
data-driven simulation models and digital twins
to evaluate alternatives and improve complex systems before changes are implemented in the real world.
Process digital twins
and automated simulation modeling
What-if analysis and scenario evaluation
Applications in
manufacturing and healthcare
Predictive & Prescriptive Analytics
We integrate
prediction, optimization, and decision support
to anticipate outcomes and determine what actions should be taken next.
Process performance prediction
Resource allocation and optimization
Data-driven operational decision support
Application Domains
Our research is grounded in real-world challenges and strengthened through long-term collaboration with
industry and public-sector partners.
Manufacturing
We apply
process mining, AI, simulation, and optimization
to semiconductor manufacturing, steel production, smart factories, and other complex manufacturing systems.
Healthcare
We develop
process intelligence, predictive analytics, and digital twins
for clinical pathways, hospital operations, patient flows, and healthcare decision support.
Fashion
We develop
AI-powered recommender systems
for personalized fashion services, including product recommendation, outfit recommendation, customer preference modeling, and intelligent curation.
From Data to Impact
Our research areas are deeply interconnected. We combine
process mining with AI
, predictions
with
optimization
, process data with
digital twins
, and recommender systems
with
generative AI
to address complex real-world problems.
Our goal is to move from data to
understanding, prediction, recommendation, innovation, and
measurable real-world impact
.

Centers and spin-offs
The lab anchors two research centres at POSTECH and two companies.
Wil van der Aalst Data & Process Science Research Center
Opened in 2024 and named after the founder of process mining, the centre anchors POSTECH's international research agenda in data and process science, hosting joint projects, visiting researchers and the Asia-Pacific Process Mining workshop series.
Future City Open Innovation Big Data Center
A POSTECH centre applying big-data and process analytics to urban problems — mobility, shrinking cities, energy use and public services — in partnership with local government.
Puzzle Data (spin-off)
Korea's first process mining software company, established as a spin-off from the lab. It brings the lab's process mining research into enterprise applications.
ZenAii Co. (spin-off)
An AI-powered fashion recommendation company spun off from the lab, translating its research in recommender systems and artificial intelligence into personalised fashion services.

Join Us — AIM Lab, POSTECH
Skip to content
Join the lab
Who we look for
Research in the lab sits between three things: a real process, the messy data it leaves behind, and a method
strong enough to say something true about both. The students who do well here enjoy all three, not just the third.
Concretely, we look for:
A background in industrial engineering, computer science, statistics, information systems or a related field
Comfort with programming — Python is the lab's working language
Curiosity about how organisations actually operate, and patience with imperfect data
Willingness to write and present in English; much of our collaboration is international
Prior experience with process mining is welcome but not expected. Most students learn it here.
Positions
Ph.D. students
Full funding through research assistantships. Ph.D. students lead a research agenda, publish at venues such as
BPM, ICPM and top information-systems journals, and typically spend time with our international partners.
M.S. students
Two-year programme combining coursework with an industry-facing research project. Many M.S. projects run
directly with a partner company and end in a deployed prototype.
대학원 입학 프로그램
Graduate admission programmes
아래 네 개 대학원 프로그램 중 하나로 진학할 수 있습니다. 지원하는 프로그램에 따라 교과 과정 및 전형 일정이
다르니, 어떤 프로그램이 맞을지 고민해 보고, 판단이 어려우면 지원 전에 먼저 문의해 주기 바랍니다.
Students enter through one of the four POSTECH graduate programmes below. Curricula and
admission schedules differ by programme, so consider which one suits you — and ask us before applying if
you are unsure.
산업경영공학과
Department of Industrial & Management Engineering
연구실이 소속된 학과입니다. 가장 일반적인 경로이며, 프로세스 마이닝과 운영·데이터 기반 의사결정을
가장 폭넓게 다룹니다.
인공지능융합대학원 (AX)
Graduate School of Artificial Intelligence Convergence
인공지능과 산업 전환이 만나는 주제 — AI 기반 프로세스 인텔리전스, 실제 운영에 적용하는
에이전틱·생성형 방법론을 다루고자 하는 경우에 적합합니다.
융합대학원 산업데이터사이언스전공 (IDS)
Industrial Data Science, Graduate School of Convergence
대규모 제조·기업 데이터를 토대로 연구를 설계하려는 학생에게 적합한 산업 지향 프로그램입니다.
국방과학기술전공 (DST)
Defense Science and Technology
분석·시뮬레이션·프로세스 인텔리전스를 국방 분야에 응용하려는 경우의 경로입니다.
How to apply
Admission is through POSTECH's graduate admissions process in one of the programmes above, but contact the lab
first — we can tell you whether there is a fit, and which programme suits you, before you invest in an
application. Write to
[이메일]
with the subject line
“Prospective student — [your name]”
and include:
A CV, including your transcript and any publications or projects
A short paragraph on which of our research areas interests you and why
Your intended start semester, degree, and which of the four admission programmes you are considering
Applications from international students are welcome. POSTECH offers graduate programmes taught in English and
supports visa and housing arrangements for admitted students.
What you get
Funded research assistantship for graduate students
Real event data from manufacturing, hospitals and public agencies
Co-authorship on international publications
Conference travel, including BPM, ICPM and INFORMS
Collaboration with the Wil van der Aalst Data & Process Science Research Center and its visitors
A strong industry placement record — Samsung, SK hynix, LG, POSCO, and academia
Frequently asked
Do I need a process-mining background?
No. A solid grounding in programming and
statistics matters more; process mining itself is taught in the lab and in POSTECH coursework.
Is the programme in English?
Graduate courses relevant to the lab are offered in
English, and lab meetings accommodate international members. Korean is useful for industry projects but not required.
Which programme should I apply to?
Industrial & Management Engineering is the
default. Choose AX, Industrial Data Science or Defense Science and Technology if its focus matches the work you
want to do — the advisor and the lab are the same either way. Ask us if you are unsure.
Is funding available?
Graduate students in the lab are supported through research
assistantships on funded projects.
Can I visit or intern?
Yes — we host visiting students and researchers, especially
through the Wil van der Aalst Data & Process Science Research Center. Write to us with your dates and interests.

http://aim.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 송민석 교수는 POSTECH 산업경영공학과 소속으로, 데이터 기반 방법론을 통해 프로세스를 이해하고 의사결정을 지원하는 AIM Lab(Analytics & Information Management Laboratory)을 이끌고 있습니다. 연구는 프로세스 마이닝, 추천 시스템, 응용 AI를 중심축으로 하며, AI 기반 프로세스 혁신, 시뮬레이션 및 디지털 트윈, 예측·처방 분석으로 확장되어 객체 중심 프로세스 마이닝, 예측적 프로세스 모니터링, 패션·콘텐츠 분야 개인화 추천, 대규모 언어모델과 생성형 AI 활용 등을 다룹니다. 주요 수행 과제로는 서울대·KAIST와 함께하는 산업통상자원부의 제조 파운데이션 모델 사업(2025.09–2029.12), 한국연구재단의 객체 중심 프로세스 마이닝 모델링·시뮬레이션·최적화 연구(2024.05–2029.04), Glocal University 30 지원의 Wil van der Aalst 데이터·프로세스 사이언스 연구센터 운영(2024.06–2028.02)이 있으며, 스마트 팩토리 운영 AI, SSF SHOP 개인화, OTT 영상 추천 등 산업 협력 과제도 진행 중입니다. 2002년 이후 46개 연구과제에 참여해 그중 37개를 연구책임자로 수행했고, 저널 논문 68편과 학회 논문 126편을 발표했으며 Expert Systems with Applications, IEEE Access, IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing 등에 교신저자로 게재했습니다. 연구 성과는 반도체 수율 요인 분석, 외래 대기시간 원인 분석 시뮬레이션 도구(MedProSim), 교통 시뮬레이션 모델 자동 생성 등 제조·의료·도시 운영 분야의 실제 문제 적용으로 이어지고 있습니다.

https://sites.google.com/view/minseokshi.summary: 신민석 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 산업경영공학과 소속으로 금융 빅데이터 분석(Financial Big Data Analysis, FBDA) 연구실을 이끌고 있습니다. 연구 관심사는 빅데이터 분석, 금융계량경제학, 리스크 관리, 고차원 통계, 시계열 분석, 고빈도 금융 등으로, 빅데이터를 위한 통계·계량 방법론을 개발해 실제 금융 문제에 적용하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 대표 성과로는 고빈도 금융데이터 기반의 적응적 로버스트 대형 변동성 행렬 추정과 두꺼운 꼬리 분포를 고려한 팩터·고유 VAR 변동성 행렬 모형 연구가 Journal of Econometrics에 게재되었고, Overnight GARCH-Itô 변동성 모형(Journal of Business & Economic Statistics), 고빈도 금융데이터의 정형화된 사실을 반영한 변동성 모형(Journal of Time Series Analysis) 등이 있으며, 고차원 시변계수 추정에 관한 논문이 Econometric Theory에 게재 예정입니다. 현재는 팩터 구조를 가진 잡음 고빈도 관측치에 대한 비볼록 고차원 시변계수 추정 등 관련 후속 연구를 진행 중입니다. 교육 면에서는 시계열 분석, 금융 빅데이터 분석 등 대학원 과목과 실험계획법 입문, 공학도를 위한 확률통계 등 학부 과목을 담당하며, 개별연구와 인턴십을 통해 정량적 배경을 갖춘 학생들을 연구실에 받고 있습니다.

POSTECH 산업경영공학과 유희천 교수가 세계인간공학협회(이하 IEA, International Ergonomics Association) 최고 등급 회원인 ‘IEA Fellow’로 선정됐다. 이는 인간공학 분야에서 탁월한 학술적 성과와 산업 현장 기여를 동시에 인정받은 것으로, 한국 인간공학 연구의 국제적 위상을 보여주는 쾌거다.
스위스 제네바에 본부를 둔 IEA는 전 세계 인간공학 학회들의 연합체로, 사람과 시스템 간 상호작용을 최적화해 삶의 질과 효율성을 높이는 것을 목표로 한다. 'IEA Fellow'는 뛰어난 연구 성과를 내거나 실질적 기여를 한 연구자에게 수여되는 최고 등급 회원 자격으로, 매년 전 세계에서 소수만 선정되는 영예다.
유희천 교수는 지난 30여 년간 인간공학과 제품 개발 분야에서 250편 이상의 논문과 다수의 특허를 발표하며 학문적 성과와 산업적 적용을 동시에 선도해 왔다. 특히 인체 측정 정보, 3D 인체 스캔 형상 처리, 디지털 인체모델 시뮬레이션 등 기술을 실제 제품 설계에 적용하며 독보적인 연구 역량을 입증했다.

EDT 연구진은 7개의 논문을 발표하였다.
(1) 횡경막 마비 환자를 위한 4D 스캐닝 기반 호흡 운동 분석 프레임워크 개발 (Xin Cui 외)
(2) 수동 들기 작업 보조를 위한 Back-Support Exoskeleton의 인간공학적 효과 평가 (정소윤 외)
(3) 지역별 특성 차이를 고려한 3D 스캔 기반 지역 특화 시트 설계 방법론 개발 (권도훈 외)
(4) XR 환경 내 인간공학적 UI 구현을 위한 설계 변수 및 인체 변수의 체계적 정리 (심고은 외)
(5) Development of a Usability Testing System Based on Extended Reality for Ergonomic Product Design (최인주 외)
(6) A Systematic Review on Digital Games Designed for Children and Adolescents with Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) (이예진 외)
(7) Strategies for Developing XR-Based Assessment and Intervention Games for Children and Adolescents with ADHD (이예진 외)

Research Areas
The Ergonomic Design Technology (EDT) Lab is dedicated to the development of novel ergonomic methodologies and solutions on engineering design problems for better harmony between humans, systems, environments. We have established collaborative relationships with various research institutions (such as the Department of Clothing and Textiles at Kyungpook National Univ., Department of Neurology at Samsung Seoul Medical Center, and Department of Clothing and Textiles at Yunsei University) and companies (such as Samsung Electronics, Korea Aerospace Industries, and Hyundai Motors) in exploring better understanding and solutions to ergonomic design problems. The major
areas of the EDT lab (see Figure 1) include: (1) digital ergonomics (computer-aided ergonomic design & evaluation), (2) ergonomic product design & development, and (3) physical interface design (human performance & workload evaluation).
Figure 1. Research areas and applications
Research Area #1: Ergonomic Product/Service Design & Development
The EDT lab has developed ergonomic designs of various products including mobile phone, vacuum cleaner, refrigerator, flame-proof clothing, flight glove, and flight suit by applying ergonomic design techniques and guidelines.
details...
contents 준비 중
Research Area #2: Digital Ergonomics
Digital ergonomics refers to the ergonomic design and evaluation of a product using humanoids in a digital environment. The digital ergonomic studies conducted in the EDT lab include helicopter cockpit design, automotive occupant packaging layout design, bus operator’s workstation design, and overhead-crane operating workstation design using Jack.
details...
contents 준비 중
Research Area #3: Human Performance and Workload Evaluation
The EDT lab has developed methodologies and measurement systems that can be applied to the design and assessment of the physical interface between a product and a user. Novel measurement and analysis systems for psychomotor performance, body motion, and hand force exertion have been developed and applied to engineering and medical research.

Dr. Liver, Virtual Liver Surgery Planning System
Co-work: Chonbuk National University Hospital
Project period: 2010.2 ~ 2013.3
Commercialized in Sept. 2012
3차원 가상 간 수술 계획 시스템인 Dr. Liver는 전북대학교 병원 의료진과 함께 복잡한 간의 해부학적 정보를 신속하고 정확하게 의사에게 제공하여 수술의 안전성과 합리성을 높일 수 있도록 개발되었다. Dr. Liver는 임상에서 의사에게 CT 영상을 기반으로 간 용적, 간 혈관 구조, 종양의 위치 및 크기, 종양 부위의 간 구역 정보 등 간 수술에 필요한 정보를 제공하여 환자의 상태를 효과적으로 분석하고 최적의 수술을 계획할 수 있게 도와 준다. 또한, Dr. Liver는 ‘간 추출→간혈관 추출→종양 진단→간 구역화→수술계획’으로 이어지는 일련의 과정을 의사들이 쉽게 수행할 수 있도록 사용자 친화적이고 절차 중심의 user interface로 설계되어 기존 외국에서 개발된 시스템들에 비해 의사가 용이하게 간 정보를 얻을 수 있도록 인간공학적으로 설계되었으며, 전북대병원, 서울아산병원, 양산부산병원, 화순전남병원 등에서 운용되고 있다.

Smart Harmony는 전자악보 상에서 노래 흐름에 따라 움직이는 timing bar에 집중하여 무선통신 기능을 가진 전자 stick을 흔들어 합주하는 음악 게임기다. 게임 참여자들이 Smart Harmony를 사용하여 친숙한 노래를 협력하여 연주함으로써 인지 능력뿐만 아니라 신체적, 사회적, 감성적 능력을 활성화시켜 두뇌 건강을 증진시키고 치매 예방에 도움이 될 수 있도록 개발되었다. Smart Harmony는 2011 국제공공디자인상과 인간공학디자인상 최우수상에 이어, 특허청 주최 ‘2011 서울국제발명전시회’에서 금상을 수상했으며, 2012년 11월에는 대한산업공학회의 제4회 산학협력 프로젝트 경진대회에서 대상을 수상하였다. Smart Harmony는 Seedtech에 기술이전 되어 2012년 9월부터 시판되고 있으며, 현재 전북대학교병원 임상센터에서 임상 효과에 대한 검증 실험을 추진하고 있다.

2007년 ~ 2008년에 수행된 한국형 기동헬기 조종실 형상 배열 및 공간 설계가 국내 최초로 개발된 한국형 기동헬기 수리온에 반영되어 체계 개발을 완료하고 육군 항공의 핵심 전력으로 사용하기 위해 양산 사업을 통해 군에 실전 배치되어 실용화되고 있다. 수리온의 개발로 우리나라는 세계 11번째 헬기 개발 국가로 진입하였으며, 상륙 기동, 의무 후송, 해상 작전 등의 후속 헬기 개발에 기반을 제공하였다. 수리온은 대당 200억원 정도에 판매되고 있으며 향후 15년간 세계 시장에 300 ~ 400대를 수출할 계획이다. 본 인간공학적 cockpit 개발은 헬기 조종사들의 인체측정, 인간공학적 심층 분석, virtual simulation, 그리고 prototype testing을 통해 이루어졌다.
Ergonomic Oxygen Mask for ROKAF pilots
Co-work: ROKAF Logistics Command
Project period: 2010.11 ~ 2012.10
Commercialized in 2015 (expected)
한국 공군 전투기 조종사의 얼굴 형태에 맞는 인간공학적 조종사 산소마스크는 공군군수사령부의 지원을 받아 공군사관학교, 경북대학교 의류학과, 그리고 산업체 일진하이테크와 공동으로 개발되었다. 현재 한국인 전투기 조종사가 착용하는 산소마스크 MBU-20/P는 미공군의 안면 측정 data를 기반으로 설계되어 한국인 조종사의 얼굴에 잘 맞지 않으며 특히 코 부위에서 심한 압박이나 산소누설이 유발되어 불편함이 있었다. 본 연구는 한국인의 안면 크기에 적합한 산소마스크 설계 개선을 위해 336명의 한국인 조종사들의 안면을 3D 측정 및 분석하고, 본 연구진에서 개발한 virtual fit assessment 방법을 기반으로 한국인 조종사의 안면 특성에 적합한 개선 산소마스크 설계를 개발한 후, 공군 조종사들을 대상으로 저압 환경 및 가속도 환경 등에서 착용성 평가 및 군 적합성 평가를 수행하여 설계 개선 효과를 검증하였다. 개선된 산소마스크는 현재 군의 시험 및 운용 평가 절차를 밟고 있고, 이후 군수품으로서의 규격 및 보급화 단계에 따라 한국 공군 조종사들에게 보급될 예정이며, 얼굴 형태가 유사한 일본을 포함한 아시아권 국가들로의 수출이 전망된다. 본 연구는 한국방위산업진흥회에서 주관하는 우수논문 공모전에서 우수 논문으로 선정되어 2013년 2월에 수상을 하였다.
Ergonomic Flight Suit Design
Co-work: Kyungpook National Univ. & Korea Air Force Academy
Project period: 2009.7 ~ 2009.12
Commercialized in 2010
인간공학적 비행복은 공군본부 지원 하에 경북대 의류학과(김희은 교수) 및 공군사관학교 시스템공학과(박세권 교수)와의 공동 연구를 통해 개발되었다. 인간공학적 비행복은 공군 전투조종사들이 착용하는 비행복에 대해 치수체계와 패턴 설계를 조종사 및 한국인 인체 측정자료를 체계적으로 적용하여 개선한 연구이다. 본 연구를 통해 기존의 불필요한 치수들을 제거하고 신규 치수들을 추가하여 치수체계의 수용율을 80%에서 96%로 향상 시켰으며, 착·탈의 편이성, 동작성, 착용감, 통기성 등을 8%~23% 향상시켰다. 개선된 비행복은 '2011 국제공공디자인상'에서 대상(인간공학 부문)과 '2011 인간공학디자인상'에서 대상을 차지했다. 본 연구를 통해 개선된 하계 비행복은 2010년 7월부터 그리고 동계 비행복은 2011년 1월부터 우리나라 조종사들에게 지급되고 있다.

삼킴장애 평가 시스템은 보건복지부의 지원을 받아 삼성의료원(나덕렬 교수), Xtron I&T, Digital Echo와 함께 Doppler 초음파 센서를 이용한 삼킴장애를 정량적으로 평가할 수 있도록 개발되었다. 삼킴 장애는 음식을 먹는 과정에서 발생하는 어려움을 포괄적으로 지칭하는 질환으로서, 뇌졸중, 중추신경 및 말초 신경을 포함하는 퇴행성 질환, 외상성 뇌질환, 두경부 종양, 근육 질환 환자 등의 여러 환자군에서 발생한다. 삼킴 장애의 심각성 정도는 질환 및 원인에 따라 차이가 있으나, 일반적으로 흡인, 폐렴, 탈수, 영양실조 등을 유발하며, 이러한 문제들이 심해지면 사망에 이를 수 있어 삼킴 장애의 과학적 진단과 치료에 대한 관심이 높다. 기존 삼킴장애 측정은 고가의 장비를 활용하고 일상 생활 중에 삼킴을 측정하는 것은 불가능해 환자들이 일상 생활 중에 겪는 삼킴 장애 특성(예: 일일 평균 삼킴 횟수, 정상 삼킴 비율)을 파악하는데 어려움이 있었다. 반면 본 장비는 저가이고 휴대가 가능하며 측정이 편리하여 환자의 삼킴 장애 정도를 일상 생활 환경 상에서 용이하게 측정하고 분석할 수 있을 것으로 기대된다. 또한, 삼킴 장애 치료 과정에서 삼킴의 인두 기능 개선 여부를 적시에 확인할 수 있어 치료 방법의 효용성 평가 및 신규 치료 방법 개발, 그리고 저주파 근육 자극기와 연동하여 효과적인 삼킴 보조 장비 개발에 유용하게 활용될 수 있을 것으로 기대 된다.

POSTECH 산업경영공학과 유희천 교수가 세계인간공학협회(이하 IEA, International Ergonomics Association) 최고 등급 회원인 ‘IEA Fellow’로 선정됐다. 이는 인간공학 분야에서 탁월한 학술적 성과와 산업 현장 기여를 동시에 인정받은 것으로, 한국 인간공학 연구의 국제적 위상을 보여주는 쾌거다.
스위스 제네바에 본부를 둔 IEA는 전 세계 인간공학 학회들의 연합체로, 사람과 시스템 간 상호작용을 최적화해 삶의 질과 효율성을 높이는 것을 목표로 한다. 'IEA Fellow'는 뛰어난 연구 성과를 내거나 실질적 기여를 한 연구자에게 수여되는 최고 등급 회원 자격으로, 매년 전 세계에서 소수만 선정되는 영예다.
유희천 교수는 지난 30여 년간 인간공학과 제품 개발 분야에서 250편 이상의 논문과 다수의 특허를 발표하며 학문적 성과와 산업적 적용을 동시에 선도해 왔다. 특히 인체 측정 정보, 3D 인체 스캔 형상 처리, 디지털 인체모델 시뮬레이션 등 기술을 실제 제품 설계에 적용하며 독보적인 연구 역량을 입증했다.

http://edt.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 유희천 교수는 포항공과대학교(POSTECH) 산업경영공학과 교수로 인간공학설계기술연구실(Ergonomic Design Technology Lab)을 이끌고 있으며, 사람과 시스템·환경의 조화를 목표로 공학 설계 문제에 적용할 인간공학 방법론과 솔루션을 개발하고 있다. 주요 연구 영역은 3D 스캔 기반 인체측정 데이터베이스 및 분석 소프트웨어(3D-ASAS, DRHM-GAS) 구축, 자동차 시트 컴포트와 운전자 피로 저감, 스마트폰·웨어러블 등 제품의 인간공학적 설계, 의료 영상 기반 간 수술 계획 및 삼킴장애 평가 기술 등이다. 대표 성과로는 전북대학교병원 의료진과 공동 개발해 2012년 상용화한 3차원 가상 간 수술 계획 시스템 'Dr. Liver', 현대자동차와의 인간공학적 버스 시트 설계가 있으며, 차량 운전자 피로 저감 시스템·스마트 비음측정기·삼킴장애 측정 치료 장치 등 국내외 특허를 보유하고 있다. 또한 기계 장치 안전을 위한 인간공학적 설계 관련 ISO 15534 시리즈 개정에 프로젝트 리더로 참여하고 있으며, 현대자동차·포스코홀딩스·한국연구재단 등이 지원하는 과제를 수행해 왔다. 2025년 1월에는 세계인간공학협회(IEA)의 최고 등급 회원인 'IEA Fellow'로 선정되었고, 2024년 산업통상자원부 장관상을 수상했다.

A mathematical approach to decision-making
Management Science (MS)
aims to improve an agent's ability to enact rational and meaningful management decisions.
Optimization
is the selection of a best element (with regard to some criterion) from some set of available alternatives.
02
Based in scientific rigor
MS
uses various
research-based
principles, strategies, and analytical methods such as mathematical modeling, statistics, and algorithms.
Optimization
strives to find
"best available"
values of a variety of objective functions given a defined domain or constraints.
03
For all kinds of business applications

https://www.msolab.org/.summary: 이강복 교수는 포스텍(POSTECH) 산업경영공학과 교수로, 경영과학·최적화 연구실(MSO Lab)을 이끌고 있으며 경영과학, 공급망관리, 조합최적화를 주요 연구 분야로 삼고 있습니다. 포스텍에서 산업공학 학사(1998)·석사(2000)·박사(2004, 운영과학)를 받았고, LG전자 생산기술원 선임연구원, 뉴욕대 스턴 경영대학원 방문연구원(박사후), 럿거스 경영대학원 연구부교수, 뉴욕시립대 York College 조교수를 거쳐 2016년 포스텍에 부임해 2023년부터 정교수로 재직 중입니다. 2023년 9월부터 포스텍 입학학생처장을 맡고 있으며, 2024년 7월부터 알고리즘·최적화센터(CALOP) 센터장을 겸하고 있습니다. 연구실 소개에 따르면 제약계획법(CP)·인공지능·OR의 통합, 생산계획 및 일정계획, 근사 알고리즘, 조합최적화를 주제로 연구하며 국제 학술지 논문 54편, 국제학술대회 논문 9편, 북챕터 2편의 실적을 보유하고 있습니다. 또한 후판 슬라브 생산 설계 장치(2023년 등록)와 연안 물류 일정계획 생성 시스템 및 방법(2025년 등록) 등 산업 현장 적용형 특허에 공동 발명자로 참여했습니다.

http://bgjang.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 장봉규 교수는 POSTECH 산업경영공학과 교수로, 금융및위험관리연구센터(ReFiRM)장과 하나-POSTECH 테크핀 산학일체연구센터장, KB-포스텍 디지털혁신연구센터장을 맡고 있습니다. 연구 분야는 투자론과 금융위험관리(자산배분, 생애주기 자산관리, 채권, 파생금융상품, 신용위험, 연금·보험사의 자산부채관리), 금융공학·금융수학·핀테크·인슈어테크, 그리고 금융 분야에 대한 기계학습 및 자연어처리 활용입니다. 대표 성과로는 Journal of Finance에 게재된 "Liquidity Premia and Transaction Costs"(2007)와 Operations Research에 게재된 "Unemployment Risks and Optimal Retirement in an Incomplete Market"(2016)이 있으며, 이 외에도 Journal of Risk and Insurance, Journal of Banking & Finance, Economic Theory, Insurance: Mathematics and Economics 등에 은퇴·연금, 재보험과 자산배분, 신용위험 모형 관련 논문을 다수 발표했습니다. 최근에는 머신러닝·딥러닝을 활용한 유가 변동성 예측, 비트코인 가격 방향 예측, 그래프 신경망 기반 기업 신용평가모형, 부채연계투자(LDI) 등으로 연구를 확장하고 있습니다. 또한 현대해상화재보험 사외이사, 산업통상자원부 방사폐기물관리기금 위험관리위원회 위원, 보험개발원 자문위원회(인슈어테크 분과), 한국해양진흥공사 리스크관리위원회 자문위원 등으로 활동하며 한국금융공학회 차기학회장을 맡고 있습니다.

보험연구원이 29일 서울 여의도 FKI타워 컨퍼런스센터 다이아몬드홀에서 ‘2026 국제 리스크·보험 워크숍(International Workshop on Risk and Insurance)’을 개최하고 인공지능(AI)·사이버 리스크, 기후변화와 극한기상, 보험 데이터 사이언스와 시장 혁신을 논의했다. 이번 행사는 포항공과대학교 , 일리노이대학교, 사이먼프레이저대학교, 보험연구원이 공동 주최했으며 국내외 보험·계리·리스크관리 전문가들이 발표와 패널토론에 참여했다.김헌수 보험연구원 원장은 축사에서 “이번 워크숍을 가능하게 한 공동 주최 기관과 관계자들에게 감사한다”며 “학계와 산업계를 연결하는 이번 행사는 예측하기 어려운 미래에 대응하기 위한 보험산업의 의지를 보여주는 자리”라고 말했다. 김 원장은 글로벌 보험산업이 중대한 전환점에 놓여 있다고 진단했다. 그는 “전통적인 리스크 패러다임은 전례 없는 기술 발전과 급격한 환경 변화 속에서 바뀌고 있다”며 “이번 프로그램은 AI 혁명과 사이버 리스크, 기후변화와 극한기상, 보험 데이터 사이언스와 시장 혁신이라는 세 가지 축을 중심으로 구성됐다”고 설명했다. 이어 “인공지능은 리스크가 구조화되고 평가되며 관리되는 방식을 근본적으로 바꾸고 있다”며 “동시에 디지털 전환은 복잡한 사이버 취약성을 동반하고 있어 즉각적이고 정교한 대응이 필요하다”고 말했다.

Cyber risk in actuarial / insurance context
Cyber risk is one of the risks that companies should be aware of. Not only can a cyber attack result in the loss of assets, but other costs such as compensation or lawsuits can also threaten the business.
Insurance can mitigate these risks through risk distribution or mutual aid. Our research into these risks includes the following:
Cyber loss prediction
Measurement of financial impact
Analysis of extreme cyber loss events
InsurTech / Digitalization in insurance
Digitalization and InsurTech are reshaping the insurance ecosystem, affecting distribution channels, customer experience, and operational efficiency.
These changes introduce both opportunities and risks, requiring new actuarial and risk management approaches. Our research into these topics includes the following:
Machine learning techniques in actuarial modeling
Study on business disruption by InsurTech
Catastrophe (extreme) risk modeling
Estimation of loss caused by extreme events is important to prevent bankruptcy. However, it is challenging due to not only lack of historical data but also continously changed system causing the events.
Our research into these risks includes the following:
Natural disaster reduction
Man-made catastrophe management
Probable maximum loss estimation
Emerging risk analysis
Insurance companies measure risk based on historical data. However, some risks, such as climate change and cyber risk, have only recently emerged, so there is no related data. These risks are called emerging risks. Our research into these risks includes the following:
Loss modelling of emerging risks
Insurance customer behaviour in the pandemic era
Digital risks as operational risks
Dependence modeling & Risk aggregation
Many statistical analyses assume that the samples are independent. However, some risks, such as the spread of infectious diseases, affect other samples, and these kinds of risk are called systemic risks.
Understanding the structures of dependency is important for correctly estimating losses. Our research into these risks includes the following:
Understanding interdependency in risks (heterogeneous risks)
Copula approaches in actuarial modelling
Risk aggregation in insurance regulatory models
Climate risk
Climate risk affects underwriting, investments, and enterprise risk management through both physical and transition channels. However, it is challenging to measure the risk due to complexity of the nature and climate change.
Our research into these risks includes the following:
Physical risk modeling (acute & chronic hazards)
Stress test under climate change
AI in insurance
AI is one of the most powerful tools for detecting nonlinear patterns in data and enhancing predictive capabilities. Recent models, such as Large Language Models (LLMs) and computer vision, are also widely used to boost productivity. However, AI also poses risks, such as uncertainty caused by complex model structures and difficulty tracking the model.
The combination of AI and insurance can contribute to the development of the insurance industry. Our research into these topics includes the following:
AI in the insurance value chain
AI-driven risk modeling
Modeling of AI risks

Systemic cyber risks and insurance regulatory capital
Systemic cyber risk can cascade across interconnected networks, generating substantial Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) losses that threaten insurers' capital adequacy. We present a framework that embeds IBNR into Solvency Capital Requirement (SCR calculations by coupling an SIR epidemic model parameterized by firms' operational resilience and sectoral network structure—with Monte Carlo simulations of loss propagation. Our analysis shows that highly resilient firms recognize losses more quickly, leading to shorter reporting periods and consequently higher IBNR in the early stages, whereas low resilient firms need longer reporting periods, causing their losses to increase over time. Sectoral comparison reveals more severe systemic impacts in finance than in information and demonstrates that large insurers maintain adequate solvency buffers while smaller insurers face solvency pressures. These findings highlight the need to incorporate IBNR, resilience, and network topology in cyber-SCR modeling.

Matrix-based Factor Analysis on the Prediction of Insurance Claims Probability
We propose a matrix-based factor analysis model for predicting the probability of insurance claims. The model employs projected principal component analysis (PPCA), which enhances the estimation of unobserved latent factors by projecting a data matrix onto a linear space spanned by insured-specific features. This approach addresses the overparameterization problem when the number of insured-specific features and insurance coverages is large, enabling more accurate estimation of claim probability than conventional methods. Using a large-scale health insurance dataset from a leading life insurer in South Korea, we demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms conventional and machine-learning benchmarks, such as logistic regression and XGBoost, in predicting claim probabilities. We further determine that our model can reduce computational time by approximately 86% and 98% compared to logistic regression and XGBoost, respectively. The proposed model provides a unified and scalable framework for modeling high-dimensional claim probabilities, offering practical value for underwriting, risk management, and personalized insurance product design.

Spatial cyber loss clusters at county level and socio-economic determinants of cyber risks
This study investigates whether cyber loss events occurring in the United States are spatially correlated and if so, which socioeconomic factors are associated with the spatial correlation. We analyze 3132 counties of the 50 U.S. states from 2005 to 2020 using the largest existing dataset of cyber risks and socioeconomic data. While previous literature found no or little spatial correlation at the state level, we are the first to document that such correlation exists at the county level; positive Moran’s I indicates that more exposed (i.e., a relatively large number of cyber events and losses) and less exposed counties are clustered. Spatial regressions show positive direct and negative indirect effects of county-level population and average income on loss frequency and severity. Large and wealthy counties thus tend to be more exposed to cyber risk events, but their geographically neighboring counties are less affected. We further investigate relatively exposed regions (California and the Northeast Coast) and three risk types (malicious, unintended, and privacy risks) and show consistent spatial effects for the key variables of population size and average income. Our findings can aid risk managers, cyber insurers, and policymakers to geographically differentiate cyber risk, recognize relatively more exposed regions, and develop more effective risk management strategies.

The effect of corporate risk management on cyber risk mitigation: Evidence from the insurance industry
We examine how corporate risk management can be used to address a firm’s vulnerability to cyber risk. We use a large, novel dataset on cyber risk and corporate risk management to analyse US insurers’ cyber loss events during the period of 2000–2021. Our analysis includes information on whether insurers have implemented an enterprise risk management (ERM) programme and whether they report applying cyber risk management (CRM). The results illustrate that the implementation of CRM measures may have no significant effect on cyber risk mitigation. However, we determine that the likelihood (frequency) of a cyber loss event decreases by 3.9% (6.8%) as ERM programmes mature year on year. We also find that an insurer can benefit from implementing both CRM and ERM through a lowered event likelihood (frequency) of 3.8 percentage points on average (3.7 percentage points) per year compared to solely implementing an ERM programme.

Optimism bias and its impact on cyber risk management decisions
This study explores how optimism bias influences decision-making in cyber risk management by developing a novel model that reflects utility loss aversion, a factor previously unexplored in this context. We find that decision-makers with self-protection as reference point are less likely to invest in other cyber risk management measures, providing support for optimism bias observed in the cyber-insurance market. We also show that decision-makers with higher loss aversion tend to not invest in other cyber risk management measures. Our results help to explain the lack of demand for cyber-insurance and have important implications for corporate risk management and public policy on cyber risk. They also help better understand cyber risk events which can trigger huge systemic consequences for economies and societies.

Optimal reinsurance with a systemic surplus shock
We examine the optimal reinsurance and asset allocation strategies for an insurer who minimizes the ruin probability and faces a systemic surplus shock. Analytically tractable solutions are obtained when this shock occurs at an uncertain time. We then demonstrate that the systemic surplus shock results in a nonstandard form of market incompleteness, which alters both qualitative and quantitative features of existing strategies without the surplus shock. In particular, a specific form of the marginal value for the insurer’s minimized ruin probability plays a key role in the characterization of optimal policies with the systemic surplus shock.

Tropical cyclone risk assessment reflecting the climate change trend: The case of South Korea
Tropical cyclones (TCs) have been one of the major natural hazards in South Korea. Increasing TC threats with significant losses have been observed over the last two decades, raising demand for better TC risk assessment in this region. However, it is observed in the literature that a comprehensive framework to help understand event features, changing climate landscape and corresponding loss results is hardly studied. To fill this gap, we propose a three-step approach to quantifying TC risks. Using historical TC records, geographic information, and socioeconomic factors, we first cluster patterns of TC hazards (i.e., track, wind speed, and precipitation) affecting South Korea. We then predict TC hazards and regional economic losses per cluster, and subsequently examine the temperature trend at the grid level, which we use to study the impact of climate change on loss prediction. The results highlight that the annual TC losses are expected to increase by 14 and 45% in the years 2050 and 2100, respectively, compared to that in 2020 and that the TC season in South Korea may last longer in future. Our findings can be useful for (re)insurers and policymakers to develop risk management schemes for regions in Korea that are more vulnerable to TC risks.

CEO political orientation, risk-taking and firm performance: Evidence from the U.S. property-liability insurance industry
We examine how CEOs’ political orientation can affect risk-taking behavior and firm performance in U.S. property-liability insurance companies. Using information on political donations made by CEOs to measure their political identity, we document a strong relationship between CEOs’ political conservatism and risk-averse behavior in insurers’ decision-making. We find that the more Republican leaning (or more politically conservative) a CEO is, the less risk a property-liability insurer tends to take in the capital market and underwriting business. We also provide evidence that insurers managed by Republican-oriented CEOs are more likely to achieve better financial profitability. The overall findings lead to the conclusion that property-liability insurers with politically conservative CEOs tend to have lower variability in their asset investments and underwriting business but are more likely to generate sufficient corporate value to satisfy their shareholders and policyholders. Unlike other relevant studies, our research attempts to address impacts of corporate governance and potential causality issues and shows that an insurer with a politically conservative CEO and more board members having multiple directorships is likely to take more risks. Our findings can offer important implications for property-liability insurers’ leadership in managing corporate risks and core business activities.

Heterogeneity in cyber loss severity and its impact on cyber risk measurement
We use the world’s largest publicly available dataset of operational risk to model cyber losses and show that the Tweedie model best fits the cyber loss severity in the financial industry. Three key determinants of loss severity are firm size, contagion risk and legal liability. We also measure the size of risk based on the estimation results and show a large degree of heterogeneity across financial firms. The results are particularly relevant with respect to the recent discussion on simplifying operational risk capital requirements and reiterate the importance of considering individual firm characteristics when modelling operational losses.

Unraveling heterogeneity in cyber risk using quantile regressions
We consider quantile regressions for adequate cyber-insurance pricing across heterogenous policyholders and calculation of claims cost associated with data breach events. We show that the impact of a firm's revenue is stronger (weaker) in the lower (upper) quantile of the cost distribution. This result suggests that mispricing may occur if small and large firms are priced using the average effect estimated by the traditional least squares approach. Using a novel dataset, our study is the first to take firm-specific security information into account. We find that firms with weaker security levels than the industry average are more likely to be exposed to large-cost events. Regarding data breaches, small or mid-size loss events are related to higher cost per breached record. We compare the premiums of a quantile-based insurance pricing scheme with those of a two-part generalized linear model and the Tweedie model to explore the usefulness of the quantile-based model in addressing heterogeneous effects of firm size. Our findings provide useful implications for cyber insurers and policymakers who wish to assess the impacts of firm-specific factors in pricing insurance and to estimate the cost of claims.

Systemic Cyber Risk and the Equilibrium Equity Premium
This study examines the asset pricing implications of systemic cyber risk. We consider an insurer exposed to systemic cyber events that jointly affect insurance losses and financial market conditions in a regime-switching economy. The insurer transfers part of its cyber exposure to financial investors through a cyber-catastrophe bond, under which investors receive fixed coupon payments while optimally choosing consumption and portfolio allocations. Using a general equilibrium framework, we show that systemic cyber risk is priced through a covariance channel in the equilibrium equity premium. The resulting risk premium depends not only on aggregate dividend risk but crucially also on the covariance between systemic cyber events and market conditions.

Catastrophe Exposure, Shocks, and Reinsurance Demand: Evidence from U.S. Property-Liability Insurers
Extant literature has documented that catastrophe risk overall drives reinsurance demand, yet it has not been addressed whether a firm’s persistent underwriting exposure to catastrophe-prone lines drives reinsurance demand temporarily with the shocks of actual disaster losses. To fill this gap, this study examines whether two dimensions of catastrophe risk—underwriting exposure and disaster shocks—each independently drive reinsurance demand. We further examine whether these responses vary with firm financial characteristics, such as capital-to-asset ratios. We analyze 17,909 firm-year observations of U.S. property-liability insurers from 1996 to 2021 using NAIC filings and SHELDUS loss data. Underwriting exposure captures each insurers concentration in catastrophe-prone lines and disaster shocks scale realized property damage by each insurer’s market share in those lines. We estimate each measure in a separate OLS specification with firm and year fixed effects. Which dimension dominates as the primary driver has direct regulatory implications—exposure-driven demand calls for ex-ante portfolio-based oversight, while shock-driven demand necessitates post-disaster buffer requirements. We find that both underwriting exposure and disaster shocks independently and positively drive the reinsurance ratio. The results also show that insurers with lower capital-to-asset ratios demand significantly more reinsurance, indicating heterogeneous reinsurance responses across insurers. Our findings are useful for regulators and risk managers who seek firm-specific, risk-based criteria for evaluating catastrophe reinsurance adequacy and supporting the long-run sustainability of property-liability insurance markets.

Do firms’ risk management activities mitigate the impact of cyber incidents?
This study investigates whether firms’ cyber risk management (CRM) activities mitigate the adverse effects of cyber incidents, which may generate substantial downside risk for firm value. We measure the impact of cyber incidents using the tail risk of firms’ stock returns, which captures changes in downside risk reflected in the stock market. Using OLS regressions, we first show that the occurrence of a cyber incident is associated with an increase in the tail risk of the affected firm’s stock returns over the post-incident period. Having established that cyber incidents increase firms’ tail risk, we next examine whether firms’ CRM activities mitigate this increase within a difference-in-difference-in-differences (DDD) framework. Using firm-level data spanning a broad cross-section of industries, we implement propensity score matching (PSM) prior to estimation in order to construct comparable treatment and control samples. The results indicate that firms engaging in CRM experience a smaller post-incident increase in tail risk than similar firms without such activities. Additional analyses by incident type reveal that the mitigating effect of CRM varies across different types of cyber incidents, suggesting that CRM is more effective in addressing some cyber risk channels than others. This heterogeneity highlights both the potential and the limitations of CRM as a firm-level risk management mechanism. Overall, the findings indicate that corporate risk management can play a substantive role in mitigating cyber-related downside risk and offer useful implications for the design of firm-level cyber risk response strategies and related policy frameworks.

Systemic Risk and Cross-Market Contagion: Market for Catastrophe Bonds with Double-Loss Triggers
Insurance-linked securities such as catastrophe (CAT) bonds are designed to transfer tail risk to capital markets, but this mechanism can fail when insured losses coincide with financial market stress. Motivated by evidence of market-level stress after major catastrophe incidents, we develop a two-regime continuous-time framework in which catastrophe-loss intensity is stochastic, and dependence between catastrophe claims and equity returns is present in the disaster regime. On the insurer’s side, the reinsurance-portfolio problem delivers closed-form regime-dependent policies and determines the maximum affordable spread for CAT bond issuance under a cost-parity benchmark. On the investor’s side, CAT bond principal losses concentrated in low-wealth states raise investors’ required spreads. Combining these two sides yields a bid-ask feasibility condition under which standard CAT bonds can fail to clear despite greater market depth. We then propose a catastrophe put option (CatPut) as a hybrid mechanism, where an insurer-funded equity-index put option is triggered only when both catastrophe and equity market thresholds are breached. We show in simulations that the CatPut can restore market clearing over a nontrivial, but layer-specific design space, implying that crisis-contingent redesign of CAT bonds can be effective in increasingly contagious risk landscapes.

Carbon regulation and ESG decoupling
This study examines how firms respond to carbon regulations in their ESG management and whether ESG ratings are properly aligned with actual emissions. Using 592 publicly listed Korean firms from 2015 to 2024, we estimate Difference-in-Differences (DiD) models with firm and year fixed effects and address staggered adoption of carbon regulations. We find evidence that the earlier Target Management System (TMS), as a weaker regulation than the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS), has no significant effect on firms’ ESG environmental scores, whereas entry into the stricter ETS is associated with a statistically significant and persistent increase in environmental scores. Yet these rating gains do not translate into real mitigation by showing no statistical evidence on a change in the rate of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction. Moreover, Granger causality tests indicate that increases in environmental scores do not precede subsequent reductions in emissions intensity. Our results suggest a decoupling between environmental scores and actual emissions outcomes after ETS entry. These findings highlight the need for regulatory designs that can induce firms to initiate measurable and verifiable reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.

Is Cyber Risk Contagion Priced? Evidence from the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
This study investigates whether investors distinguish between contagious and non-contagious cyber risks in the cross-section of stock returns. Although recent literature establishes cyber risk as a priced factor in financial markets, asset pricing theory predicts that only its non-diversifiable component should command a risk premium, suggesting that the key dimension is not cyber risk broadly, but its potential for systemic propagation. We propose a novel text-based framework using a transformer-based language model to classify contagious cyber incidents and estimate firm-level ex-ante exposure via a machine learning algorithm. Our event-study analysis reveals that contagious incidents are associated with significantly larger and more persistent negative abnormal returns over an extended event windows, with these effects particularly pronounced for highly leveraged firms. Firms with higher exposure to contagious cyber risks earn a significant positive risk premium of approximately 33 basis points per month, whereas exposure to non-contagious risk is not priced. We conclude that investors selectively price cyber risk, identifying contagion as the primary channel through which cyber threats become a systematic, non-diversifiable risk factor.

Heterogeneous Insurance Demand Regimes in SMEs: The Roles of Managerial Preferences and Financial Constraints
We examine how managerial preferences, internal risk-control practices, and financial frictions jointly shape insurance demand among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Using a unique dataset of 693 Korean SMEs that links 2023 survey measures of managerial risk aversion and risk-control orientation with 2020-2022 financial statements, we estimate baseline OLS models, a nonlinear CEO-ownership threshold model, and finite mixture regressions to capture latent heterogeneity in insurance-demand behavior. The OLS results show that SMEs led by more risk-averse managers purchase significantly more discretionary insurance, and that internal risk-control activities complement rather than substitute for insurance. Insurance demand also rises with tax incentives and financial constraints but declines with firm size. Threshold estimation reveals a non-monotonic ownership effect: insurance demand decreases with CEO ownership below 37% but increases beyond it. Finite mixture models uncover three distinct behavioral regimes - reference-and-control, preference-only, and financial-driven -each characterized by different mechanisms linking preferences, controls, and financial conditions to insurance purchases. These findings demonstrate that SMEs do not follow a single representative demand rule and that pooled estimates obscure economically meaningful heterogeneity. The results offer implications for targeted insurance design, SME risk-management policy, and credit-risk assessment.

Firm-specific cyber vulnerability and basis risk reduction in cyber parametric insurance: A dynamic factor model approach
Traditional indemnity-based cyber insurance struggles to keep pace with the escalating frequency and complexity of cyber threats, resulting in a widening protection gap for industry. To address this, we propose a novel cyber parametric insurance framework based on firm-specific cyber vulnerability that is estimated using a dynamic factor model incorporating geographic location, firm size, and industry sector. Our framework helps cyber insurers reduce basis risk by accounting for temporal dynamics and firm heterogeneity into cyber risk assessment. It can also facilitate to tailor a risk mitigation solution by considering substantial variations in corporate vulnerability that is integrated into the parametric index with the duration of cyberattacks. We provide supporting evidence on this benefit of the proposed framework by demonstrating a reduction in basis risk of our parametric insurance without increasing insolvency, compared to a benchmark. This study can contribute to the development of sustainable and scalable cyber parametric insurance markets.

Global Economic Fragmentation and Insurance Industry Risk (세계경제의 분절화와 보험산업 리스크)
This article argues that geo-economic fragmentation — the IMF's term for the policy-driven reversal of decades of global economic integration — has become a structural feature of the world economy rather than a passing disruption, and that it now transmits systematically into insurance industry risk. Using recent episodes such as Red Sea shipping reroutes and critical-mineral export controls as illustrations, the author distinguishes fragmentation from ordinary market-driven change: it originates in deliberate policy motivated by security and strategic competition, and it propagates through trade, capital flows, labor mobility, technology, payments, and global initiatives like climate cooperation. The article traces three transmission channels into insurance. First, supply-chain disruption, as reshoring and friend-shoring raise transitional uncertainty, alter marine/cargo and business-interruption exposures, and create correlated losses across nominally independent contracts — while also generating new demand for political-risk, cyber, and renewable-energy coverage. Second, macroeconomic and interest-rate effects, where persistent inflation and "higher for longer" rate volatility strain life insurers' asset-liability management, FX hedging, and sovereign-bond holdings, and policy uncertainty depresses life insurance penetration specifically. Third, the erosion of risk diversification itself, as constrained cross-border reinsurance narrows risk pools, diverging regulation burdens multinational insurers, and weakened international cooperation threatens the insurability of systemic risks like climate change. The article concludes that because fragmentation's ultimate trajectory cannot be forecast, insurers' priority should be preparedness rather than prediction — internalizing geopolitical risk within enterprise risk management and reinforcing capital and reinsurance strategies — so the industry can continue functioning as a genuine shock absorber for an increasingly uncertain global economy.

From Ownership to Experience: The Normalization of Subscription and the Paradigm Shift in the Insurance Market (구독의 일상화와 보험시장의 패러다임 전환)
This article argues that the rise of the subscription economy is prompting a paradigm shift in the insurance industry, as consumption shifts from one-time ownership to continuous, personalized experience. While traditional insurance fixes coverage and terms at the point of contract and maintains limited contact with policyholders outside of claims, subscription-based insurance—or "Insurance-as-a-Service"—embeds insurance within a recurring payment relationship characterized by flexible digital enrollment, real-time coverage adjustment, and data-driven personalization. The article classifies subscription insurance into curation-type services, where consumers or insurers configure coverage bundles, and premium-benefit-type services, which combine coverage with embedded partnerships or value-added risk-management offerings, illustrating each with international cases such as Liberty Mutual, Lemonade, Asurion, igloo, Vitality, and Oscar Health. It then identifies the domestic regulatory barriers to adoption in Korea, spanning disclosure obligations, dark-pattern regulation, special-benefit prohibitions, underwriting design, and data governance, and proposes a phased roadmap—beginning with low-risk embedded models, advancing through regulatory-sandbox piloting of curation services, and culminating in institutionally supported value-added offerings. It concludes that subscription-based insurance can help insurers overcome stagnant growth, particularly in life insurance, by lowering entry barriers and sustaining lifecycle-long customer engagement.

The AI Industry Supercycle, the Changing Risk Landscape, and Challenges for Insurance (인공지능 산업 슈퍼사이클, 리스크 환경 변화, 그리고 보험의 과제)
This article argues that the rapid diffusion of generative and agentic AI is transforming AI from a business tool into core industrial infrastructure, creating new and more complex risks for insurers. AI-related losses are no longer limited to inaccurate predictions or hallucinated outputs; with agentic AI, errors can directly trigger wrong transactions, system changes, business interruption, liability claims, cyber incidents, regulatory violations, reputational damage, and even physical losses. The article classifies AI risks into technology and operational failure, cybersecurity and privacy, legal and ethical liability, reputation and organizational capability, and sustainability risks, then explains how these become insurance losses through triggers such as internal-control failure, direct AI execution, system contagion, external manipulation, rights infringement, and physical operation. It concludes that AI risk is not inherently uninsurable, but insurers must clarify liability across the AI value chain, strengthen underwriting around governance and control points, manage accumulation risk, refine AI exclusions, expand existing insurance coverage, and gradually develop stand-alone AI insurance as data and scenario-based pricing methods mature.

Institutional Challenges and Strategic Responses for Artificial Intelligence in the Insurance Industry (보험산업과 인공지능(下): 제도적 과제와 전략)
This article examines the institutional and strategic issues surrounding the adoption of artificial intelligence in the insurance industry, with a particular focus on the Korean insurance market. It argues that although AI has significant potential to enhance underwriting, claims handling, customer service, fraud detection, and asset management, its practical use remains constrained by regulatory ambiguity, fragmented data infrastructure, weak governance systems, and concerns over algorithmic accountability, privacy, fairness, and consumer protection. The discussion identifies major risk categories associated with AI adoption, including errors in decision-making, discrimination and bias, personal-information leakage, cybersecurity threats, and uncertainty over responsibility when automated systems cause harm. In response, the article proposes a policy framework that clarifies legal responsibility, strengthens data-sharing and verification systems, promotes model transparency, and establishes governance standards suitable for insurance-specific AI applications. It further suggests that insurers should adopt AI gradually across the value chain by prioritizing high-impact and low-risk use cases, building internal data and compliance capabilities, and coordinating technological innovation with regulatory readiness. Overall, the article concludes that sustainable AI transformation in insurance requires not only technological investment but also institutional reform, risk-control mechanisms, and strategic implementation aligned with consumer trust and market stability.
