ABOUT LAB
Lab
Media
Alloy Design Lab specializes in analyzing the microstructure of materials to identify the correlations among different characterization factors.
Through the utilization of diverse analytical techniques, including various microscopy methods and theoretical calculations, our primary goal is to comprehend the relationship between
properties that emerge at the microstructural level and those exhibited at the macro level when materials are in their bulk state.

Alloy Design
Since the various combinations of strength and ductility can be achieved in steel, they have found extensive applications across diverse environments. A wide range of mechanical properties can be obtained depending on the alloy compositions and heat treatment processes (temperature, time, and cooling conditions…). We design the alloy compositions and optimize the heat treatment schedule to achieve the desirable mechanical properties. We perform detailed microstructure analyses with these works to understand their new mechanical response. This comprehensive approach enables us to tailor steel production precisely for the intended applications.

Fracture in extreme temperature condition
Fracture of steel in cryogenic and high-temperature environments is a critical issue in applications for extreme temperature conditions. We are researching the main reasons of fracture in extreme temperature conditions (cryogenic (~20 K) and high-temperature (> 800
℃
)). We aim to enhance our understanding of steel’s behavior in these demanding environments by investigating fracture mechanisms and characterizing microstructural changes. Furthermore, we try to suggest some methods to prevent the brittle fracture in extreme temperature conditions.
Improved hot ductility of TWIP steel via MnS inoculation
Improved hot ductility of high-Ni steel via recrystallization after diffusionless transformation
Brittle fracture (intergranular and cleavage fracture)
Brittle fractures can be divided into intergranular(IG) and cleavage fractures according to crack propagation paths.
IG fractures in steels are generally related to the local segregation of impurities or precipitation of hard phases at the grain or phase boundary. The segregation behavior at the grain boundaries is not simply associated with exposing temperature and time but is complexly correlated with precipitation behaviors in a matrix and at the grain boundaries. We are researching the correlation between precipitation and segregation and trying to suggest mitigation strategies in various steel, such as lightweight steel, maraging steel, and bcc steel. Cleavage fracture is related to the relative strength difference between theoretical cleavage strength and shear strength. Thus, we investigate intrinsic modulus changes depending on alloying elements to clarify cleavage fracture.
The intergranular fracture after aging by intermetallic compounds precipitation in maraging steel
The intergranular fracture by S segregation in the steel

Advanced Microstructure Characterization
The steel’s properties and performance can be interpreted by microstructure characterization through detailed examination and microscale analysis. It encompasses studying various microstructural features, such as grain boundaries, phases, and crystal defects. By utilizing advanced techniques such as in-situ experiments (in-situ tensile, in-situ heating) and atomic level characterization with Cs-corrected TEM, we are researching to find and interpret veiled mechanisms in various steel, such as TRIP steel, lightweight steel, maraging steel, and so on.
The microstructure evolution of TRIP steels with different cooling rate during tensile test
The formation of inverse-spinel MnAl2O4 in lightweight steel
The evolution of ledge-typed twin boundary in bcc steel
Surface characterization
In the automotive industry, reducing the weight of automobiles has been conducted to increase fuel efficiency. Since this endeavor has led to the substitution with high-strength steel, guaranteeing the corrosion resistance of high-strength steel sheets becomes pivotal in extending the quality assurance period. The corrosion resistance can be enhanced by additional coating, such as painting and conversion coating, and the coating quality is determined by surface characteristics. Therefore, we are researching the correlation of surface characteristics (surface microstructure, surface composition) with surface defects or coating quality. Also, through various methods, modifying surface characteristics to prevent the surface defect or to enhance the coating quality are conducted.

http://adl.postech.ac.kr/.summary: 허윤욱 교수는 포항공대(POSTECH) 철강대학원 소속으로 합금설계연구실(ADL, Alloy Design Laboratory)을 이끌고 있습니다. 연구실의 주요 연구 분야는 합금 설계(Alloy Design), 파괴 거동(Fracture Behavior), 미세조직 분석(Microstructure Characterization) 세 축으로 구성되어 있으며, 합금 조성과 열처리 조건(온도·시간·냉각조건)을 제어해 목표 기계적 물성을 구현하는 연구를 수행합니다. 파괴 거동 분야에서는 조성, 편석, 석출 등이 취성 파괴에 미치는 영향과 극저온(약 20 K) 및 고온(800℃ 이상) 등 극한 환경에서의 철강 파괴 원인을 규명하고 있습니다. 미세조직 분석에서는 in-situ 인장·가열 실험과 수차보정(Cs-corrected) TEM을 활용한 원자 수준 분석으로 결정립계, 상, 결함 등을 연구합니다. 또한 페라이트계 고Si 강과 오스테나이트계 고Mn 강의 열응력 형성 및 열간 균열 생성 기구에 관한 논문(Materials Science and Engineering: A 투고)에 교신저자로 참여하는 등 철강 소재 관련 연구 성과를 발표하고 있습니다.

Research Theme
Battery performance cannot be understood from a single material, length scale, or measurement. Our research connects atomic structure, interfacial chemistry, reaction dynamics, particle evolution, and electrode behavior to uncover the principles governing real batteries—and to translate them into better materials and electrodes.
We do not study materials, interfaces, and electrodes as separate systems.
We connect them to reveal how batteries actually work—and how they can be designed better.
Contents
Theme 1. Advanced Cathode Materials for Li- and Na-ion Batteries
Theme 2. Disorder-Enabled and Emerging Cathode Chemistry
Theme 3. Electrochemical Interfaces and Interphases
Theme 4. Multiscale Reaction Dynamics
Theme 5. Dynamics-Informed Electrode Design
Theme 6. Synchrotron-Enabled Multiscale Characterization

"From hidden battery dynamics  to materials and electrode design"
We study rechargeable Li/Na batteries across atomic, interfacial, particle, and electrode scales.
By revealing the mechanisms that govern Li/Na transport, charge transfer, reaction heterogeneity, and degradation.
we aim to establish design principles for next-generation energy storage materials.

Innovative Energy Materials Laboratory
POSTECH
"From hidden battery dynamics  to materials and electrode design"
We study rechargeable Li/Na batteries across atomic, interfacial, particle, and electrode scales.
By revealing the mechanisms that govern Li/Na transport, charge transfer, reaction heterogeneity, and degradation.
we aim to establish design principles for next-generation energy storage materials.
Jihyun Hong lab, Jihyun Hong group at POSTECH

Principal Investigator
Jihyun Hong
| Associate Professor at POSTECH | Battery Materials
I am a materials scientist investigating innovative electrochemical energy storage materials and systems for a greener society, with relevant experiences in materials design, synthesis, and analysis.
I am particularly interested in fundamental problems related to structural evolution and charge transfer reactions of practically important materials under real-life situations involving non-equilibrium and dynamic conditions. I acknowledge wisdom and knowledge from collaborations and try to cultivate diverse ideas and cultures in the group.

Innovative Energy Materials Laboratory
POSTECH
"From hidden battery dynamics  to materials and electrode design"
We study rechargeable Li/Na batteries across atomic, interfacial, particle, and electrode scales.
By revealing the mechanisms that govern Li/Na transport, charge transfer, reaction heterogeneity, and degradation.
we aim to establish design principles for next-generation energy storage materials.

https://ieml.postech.ac.kr.summary: 홍지현 교수는 POSTECH 부교수로 재직하며 Innovative Energy Materials Laboratory(IEML)를 이끄는 배터리 소재 분야 연구책임자입니다. 리튬·나트륨 이차전지를 원자, 계면, 입자, 전극 등 여러 스케일에 걸쳐 연구하며, Li/Na 이온 수송, 전하 전달, 반응 불균일성, 열화 메커니즘을 규명해 차세대 에너지 저장 소재의 설계 원리를 제시하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 대표 성과로는 리튬 과잉 층상 산화물의 경로 의존적 질서-무질서 상 전이를 통합적으로 설명한 연구를 교신저자로 Energy & Environmental Science(2026)에 발표했으며, 해당 논문은 inside front cover로 선정되었습니다. 또한 Advanced Energy Materials, Angewandte Chemie 등 학술지의 표지 논문 실적과 함께, 리튬이차전지용 양극 활물질 및 양극활물질 조성물 관련 특허를 다수 출원했습니다. 연구실은 이차전지 소재과학에 관심 있는 대학원생과 박사후연구원을 상시 모집하고 있습니다.
